reviews.title: Fast-Moving, Graphic Thriller With Comic "Keystone Kops" Moments
reviews.body:
THE CONTRACTORS is a highly entertaining, fast-paced, at-times-gruesome thriller that makes some intriguing, possibly true-to-life, rather disturbing points about the wisdom of any U.S. government decision to employ private DEA contractors to save money.

As Jon Cantrell, a contract DEA operative, learns in this novel, you can't trust individual contract operatives, because contracting companies sometimes hire their mercenaries (no background checks required!) from the absolute dregs of society.  And you can't trust contracting companies, because their orders may be coming from government employees in overlapping jurisdictions (ignorance of other operations is bliss!), or from crooked government employees with private agendas (recover a missing cartel witness and kill her! or recover a missing cartel witness and save her because she's your lover!).  And it's bad news (likely to end in death!) for decent, honest contract operatives, government employees, and civilians alike, when the government hands over to private contractors the latest military hardware (guns and giant long-range rifles!) or cutting-edge surveillance scanning devices (read auto battery bar codes and instantly identify and track drivers!).

If it weren't for the many killings, usually described in gruesome detail, this book could almost be described as a "rollicking adventure".  At times it has a comic "Keystone Kops" feeling, as competing contract companies repeatedly disrupt their competitors' operations (by intention, inadvertence, or total incompetence), and as Jon and his hard-boiled female partner (Piper) escape certain-death situations again and again due to some bizarre ricochet or convenient hidden pathway or suddenly available transport.

This novel is a creative blend of interesting characters (e.g., Jon, Piper, Sinclair the cop on the take, Eva the cartel witness on the lam, Milo the can-do crook, Kevin the drug-addled DEA operative, McNally the deal-closing Senator); of wildly outlandish plot developments; and of particularly brutal deaths for the bad guys.  In the end, it all melds into a satisfying whole, with a surprising but nevertheless believable ending.  I'm looking forward to reading more standalone thrillers like this one from author Harry Hunsicker!

reviews.title: from the gritty side of Dallas to a blood soaked finish in Marfa, West Texas
reviews.body: Jon Cantrell is a really good guy who has had a streak of bad luck. He's a disgraced ex-cop working for military contractors as a Department of Justice Drug Enforcement Agent in Dallas, Texas.  Cantrell and his partner, Piper, (they are also friends with benefits) are hired by Captain Sinclair, a retired Dallas police officer, to confiscate a drug shipment. Instead, they score a witness,  Eva Ramirez, in a drug cartel court case that could bring down the largest criminal organization in North America. Their Mission Impossible is to transport the witness to the US District Attorney, simple enough if it weren't for the uncooperative witness, corrupt cops and the hit that is out on all of them. I especially like the humor that gives you a break from all the bleak. Plenty of twists and betrayals along the way.

reviews.title: Not for me - weak & overwrought females, feels derivative of other similar books
reviews.body:
I am new to Harry Hunsicker and The Contractors was not the best introduction to his work. Make no mistake, I LOVE a good shoot 'em up story and I really love a good chase story - especially when it rolls through West Texas, so I was excited to pick this book up and looked forward to settling in for weekend immersed in a thriller I could not put down. It was not to be. This book is about 200 pages too long with ten characters too many and frankly I kept stopping to do other things and finding myself not caring if I picked it back up or not.

The good things were very good - the author knows Texas fairly well and has clearly read a map and traveled some of our back roads, so kudos there. The action scenes, when they finally showed up, were tight and pretty well done and the weapon descriptions and use by the various actors was correct and plausible. My interest began to wane significantly very early though with the introduction of Piper, our hero Jon Cantrell's lover and partner. This woman was so weak, so over burdened by emotional baggage and thus rendered unstable and irrational that she would never be suitable or even reasonably considered for a position as federal contractor, much less a working partner to a guy we're supposed to believe is a good agent/contractor former cop. I just could not suspend belief long enough to accept that Cantrell didn't want to kill Piper himself as much as I did.

It was about the three quarter mark that I realized I was having a faint dejavu moment and why with this entire book. It totally reminded me of both In the Electric Mist and No Country For Old Men! Both of which were done years earlier and worth five stars all day long for so many reasons.

reviews.title: One big complex family and a love interest.
reviews.body: Crazy obstacles that get solved with a lot of infighting. The romance doesn't build so much as inflates and deflates relentlessly.  I am a romantic suspense junkie so I loved it but if you are looking for anything along the lines of a police procedural than stay away or you will feel like a blithering idiot by the halfway point, becuase it's a fun read but goes on and on without solving the inital problem.

reviews.title: Too long, too much, no thrills,  not enough mystery or suspense.
reviews.body:
I read everything, but if an author is going to write a book this long, it's really got to give me a reason to hang in there until the bitter end.  I felt that an editor could have carved 150-200 pages out of this novel and still had a good story.  Too often, the plot got bogged down in pages of information that didn't add to the reading experience.

The protagonist doesn't seem to have a friend in the world (except his team members) so  we're always evading someone - the mob, the FBI, etc.  With complicated plot lines, characters I didn't care that much about, and non-stop action which wasn't that much fun to read about,  Do or Die fell far short of a fun read.  It was laborious.  I wish I could have been with the majority on this one, because so many kudoes can't be wrong!  Read it and make up your own mind!

reviews.title: For the love of family. 3.5-4 stars
reviews.body:
For the last year, Ian Dunn has sacrificed his freedom..literally sitting in prison ....doing time for something that he didn't do. But being the big brother that he is, he will do anything if it means keeping those he loves safe. So when a group wants to free him from prison in order to use skills to rescue the children of a nuclear physicist, his entire plan appears to be going up in smoke.  Playing hard ball are two lawyers, the  feisty Phoebe Kruger and determined Martell Griffin, who can't for the life of them figure out why Ian doesn't want to play ball. As the stakes grow even higher and the danger mounts, Ian must free the kids, elude the mob, fight his growing attraction to Phoebe and save his brother before the week is out, all with the help of his ex-team, who are equally fascinating and have a back story of their own.

While "Do or Die" is the typical Brockmann story, there is a ton of stuff to like. There is espionage, intrigue, danger, gun fights, bombs, good guys, bad guys and romance. You even see a few of the characters from the "Troubleshooter" series.  My only criticism is that it was a tad bit slow in areas. While there was danger, there were also a few parts that seemed to stretch on and on when it was not necessary. On the other hand, there were times that  I wanted a little more, but instead was left a little confused and let down. Overall, this was a decent read, hence the 3.5-4 star rating. Honestly, I think if you enjoy Brockmann's other works, you'll enjoy this one too. Regardless, it seems to be a promising beginning to a pretty decent series.

reviews.title: Okay
reviews.body: The Baddest Girl on the Planet starts out slowly. It took a while for me to get into it. The first half of the book took me about a week, but the last half I finished in an afternoon. The chapters jump around a lot. It's not a story that goes in a linear order, or at least it wasn't any order that I could tell.  Each chapter was more of a chunk of Evie Austin's life. I didn't care much for Evie until the last third or so of the book. The writing was good. There were a lot of descriptive pieces. Overall, I found it to be okay. I didn't dislike it but I didn't love it either.

reviews.title: When Good Girls Go Bad 🕶
reviews.body:
Ruined reputations and revenge... When 5-year-old Austin is the only remaining link between a stay-at-home, absentee father and a headstrong, young divorcée mom, things are bound to get tense on Hatteras Island. Tempers flare, patience is tested, and some of the most mundane sections of dialogue become undeniably humorous in the moment — “Then you’ll just have to eat bologna.” We’ve all had our moments of accepted defeat, and these characters seem so genuinely authentic.

Readers will encounter mentions of childhood memories involving campsites, imaginary dogs, pirate stories, and a lighthouse relocation. Throughout the story, relationships are tested and friendships are pushed to the breaking point. Clever passages of descriptive rhetoric give some flavorful spark to illicit lovers, funeral services, tropical vacations, and Irish pen pals, and I definitely laughed at dog Walter (the Yorkshire terrorist). I found some of the horrifically accurate adventures in infant care comically entertaining, and other young mothers would be equally enthralled by the chaotic mishaps. The raw honesty throughout this book was relatable and refreshing!

reviews.title: Something different!
reviews.body:
If you are an eclectic reader, always looking for something unusual to read - a different setting, different characters, and a different treatment of the content of the novel - here it is!  Here, you’ll be treated to Evie Austin, who talks about her life - always in the first person - so that you will see and feel her experiences sitting beside her like her best friend!  Evie’s tales and traumas are presented in thirteen chapters - each of which could stand alone as a short story!

Evie explains her childhood as a nine year old living in the Outer Banks - but goes on to treat us to life as a divorced mother of a son, Austin - and, no, she didn’t name her son, Austin Austin (inside joke).  Her stories are laced with brutal truth, humor, pathos and are always detailed with descriptions that sing. Evie doesn’t mince words - she always lets us know exactly how she feels!

Yes, this novel novel is different, but very easy to get used to - and, you will not want it to end. The publisher probably snapped this up as a worthy choice for the “chick-lit” millennial  audience - but this grandmother loved its honesty and the humorous, often times “laugh out loud” funny thoughts on Evie’s mind!  I’ll be watching and waiting for Heather Frese’s next!

reviews.title: Still good after all these years
reviews.body: My grandson just turned 3 and is really loving having stories read to him as he learns to read himself.  Can you ever go wrong with Dr. Suess??  I don't think so.  Dr. Suess has a great way of "speaking" to imaginations.  Highly recommend all.

reviews.title: This is the first book I learned to read by myself.  Now it's for my grandson
reviews.body: Would have been perfect except they inserted the book upside down from the bindings so it had to  be returned and a new one was sent.  This is very high drama for a young child - poor baby bird trying to find it's mother. But its such a relief when he finally does! One of the best childrens books ever written,

reviews.title: Meh
reviews.body: I have an iphone and needed to learn to take better pictures. I began by reading through some of the hints in the book while looking on my phone. When I was ready to try the hints..I didnt have the button choice they were talking about..lol I did the list..opened the camera, click on the arrows to change the lens to take a selfie..so far so good..I was then to look for the " selfie" choice to take the photo but its not on my phone lol  I scrolled through everything.. I can take a regular selfie on " photo" but not like they say..guess Im dumber than other dummies... But thereis a lot of useful info maybe if you have a newer model.

reviews.title: Good, High Level, Overview of Iphone Photography
reviews.body: This book ended up being rewarding for us.  I was expecting a reference of buttons and options with a few nice tips and it was pretty much that, but also with a lot of photography, lighting and compositional hints added in.  I did learn a couple of things about turning off live mode and using the side buttons for releasing the shudder, but that part was just the first 60 pages.  Beyond that it breaks up into genres of photography from landscapes and travel to sports and product photography.  Each area gives some solid general tips, but also shows how to get the most out of your iphone.  It is filled with hints like switching to portrait modes to narrow the depth of field, but also has some questionable "help" with things like how to pick the right fanny pack for travel.  But all in all, We found this read well worth it.

reviews.title: An Unusually thought Provoking book by a Great Author
reviews.body:
Some number of years ago, I stumbled across Daniel Silva's first book. Now my summer is not complete without reading the latest one.

This book is one of his best. It concerns the characters and Jewish history more than his others. The Allon related events are more of the moment than the long planned ones we are accustomed to.

But, the suspense is great. I could not put the book down. The characters are more real than before and; at the end, the world is once again safe.

I have always wished Mr. Silva could write more than one book a year. But, I guess he chooses not to. So, now I await next summer and the next book he writes. I look forward to reading it.

reviews.title: Four Stars
reviews.body: Not as developed as Stephanie but I like the characters so far.

reviews.title: "The scariest monsters have the best masks." Bloody Mary.
reviews.body:
Lt. Jacqueline 'Jack' Daniels has a lot on her plate: her mom is getting old and refuses her help; her boyfriend wants a commitment; her partner is on another diet and Viagra; she's recently acquired a neurotic cat; her obnoxious ex-partner (who portrayed her as a fat inept detective in his movie) has returned to annoy her; and to make matters worse she's trying to catch a serial killer who leaves body parts with things that belong to her. As Jack and her partner search for the truth, they are startled to find the unthinkable, that one of their own (a police officer)might be responsible.

This was my first Konrath novel and I'm sure it won't be my last. This was the perfect mystery novel....there was romance; a serial killer; a decent plot and tons of humor. I highly recommend it.

reviews.title: Awesome Legal Thriller
reviews.body: This is a great legal thriller. The author is new to me . Started reading "Dark Moon" first of a four book series.  Bought the other books in this series.  A good legal thriller series.

reviews.title: A surprisingly good debut!
reviews.body:
This is a fascinating debut novel - and a masterful handling of a difficult plot as a first venture into the literary world.  It takes a bit to get into the theme of it, but, it's worth the effort to stay with it, as, little by little, everything falls into place.  I always take a deep breath when encountering a novel that flips back and forth between present day and chapters of the past  and, in this case, I did have to go back and check a number of times to keep track.  I am getting used to this back and forth showing up in so many novels that my "whiplash" was minimal in THE GOOD LIAR!

Since we meet the main characters as elderly, there is a lot of past life to report, and in Roy's case, it all adds up to the person he is in the present.  You will be amazed that he can live a life of lie upon lie and get away with it.  Betty has an interesting and relevent past as well, and the author weaves everything together with great skill.

At times. gripping and difficult to put down, this novel is a great first effort by Searle.  I have no doubt that he will emerge as a popular writer, known for his creativity.  I'll look forward to his next novel.

reviews.title: Expected more on the development and making of the product
reviews.body: Starts off well but then goes  too far into the esoteric and meaning of life aspect.  This is especially true from the authors perspective.  You have three generations of whiskey makers but really need more focus on the product, manufacturing, equipment and marketing.  The author is too self involved and found myself skipping his monologue on the meaning of life.  It should be about great bourbon.

reviews.title: Ha! On me!  I thought this was a cookbook!
reviews.body:
Lucky for me it's more than a cookbook.

The story of a modern Daniel Boone, growing up in Michigan, one of three sons of a hunter.  Beginning at age eight when he shot a squirrel, to age 13 his first deer, then hunting his way through college, a career as a fur trapper, hunting sheep in Alaska, canoeing the Missouri River for deer and ending in Brooklyn age 37. Brooklyn?

I especially liked that I share his disgust at catch & release fishing - if you fish it, you have to eat it - anything else is sadism (my words).

My brother in law is the cook in the family and I wanted to see if this would be a good gift for him and I struck pay dirt following each chapter are "Tasting Notes" where the author speaks of cooking wild game.

I also enjoyed it for the history of the land he has hunted as well as the history of the hunt (I too was a big Daniel Boone fan growing up!).

I think more pictures (everything but dead things) would have made this a keeper.

reviews.title: Sad, funny, interesting - a great, too short read!
reviews.body:
This book was a big surprise in that it was everything a novel is supposed to be - great characters, interesting settings, and a plot that holds interest and turns pages.  I wasn't sure when I started it, but soon got used to the diary entries, and, in no time, I was arm in arm with the protagonist.  The story was sweet, poignant, sad, funny, frustrating - all the things that rise to the surface when a family member is starting the slide into dementia.
The poignancy came in when the father, despite his lack of recall of everyday things, could remember in great detail, his special times with his daughter.  And, she found his recollections appearing, written beautifully, as the days and months progressed.

The pages just rolled by, and I was sad to see the story end - it had become so real, that at times, I was sure I was reading a memoir.  I wanted to know about the future of all the characters.  It's a short novel and once you get going, you'll set a speed record for finishing a book.

Great read!

reviews.title: No disappointment here! Vince and Elle will touch your heart.
reviews.body: Disclaimer first: I received an ARC of this story in exchange for an honest review. Now the good stuff, but no spoilers. I LOVE Willow Winters' writing. This is the second in the Valetti Crime Family series and I hope she keeps them coming! Vince is a mobster who is keeping an eye on things in the local mob-owned bistro. Elle is a college student looking for a place where she can study in peace away from her abusive, alcoholic mother. They are immediately attracted to each other physically. Her air of shy innocence just draws Vince in deeper. After their intimate encounter in the back office of the bistro, she feels since it is over, she should leave ASAP. Vince is not ready for the encounter to be over and chases after her. Unfortunately, choosing door #1 to escape through is the absolute wrong choice and she sees what should be left unseen. Rules are rules and Vince knows what must happen to his 'sweetheart.' Can Vince do what he knows must be done or is Elle too important to him for him to be able to follow the rules of la familia? This story of the choices this tough guy has to make is tempered by the love of and for a type of woman he has never met before. There is no cliffhanger and they get their HEA.

reviews.title: I enjoy all Phil Rickman's books.
reviews.body:
Merrily Watkins and all her fellows in the books are fun and fully-fleshed people.  Rickman captures the flavor of the English and Welsh borderlands.
My only criticism of his writing is that when he changes from the POV of one character to another, you can't always tell immediately.  As an editor, I would like a little white space or some sort of break on the page so that the paragraphs don't all just run together.

reviews.title: Good entertaining read.
reviews.body:
Over all this book is a good entertaining read. The first half of the book does feel slow. Definitely not a page turner that you would finish in one night. The 2nd half is more fluid. I can see a movie made on this one as well.
Just wished that the kids would show more emotions by the end of the book. But it didn't happen.

reviews.title: BEAUTIFULLY CREATED * SUMPTUOUS RECIPIES * SOURCING PAGES
reviews.body: Treated Myself to this Adeena’ s Latest Cookbook to include her healthy & fresh recipes into my new lifestyle of the same way of eating. This is hands down best cookbook I have ever own. Recipes are enchantingly easy to follow & Adeena has thoughtfully included pages 358 & 359 as Listed Shopping 🛒 Guide as to find the specialty spices, items in her recipes, Whole Foods & some via online suppliers ; so even in Pandemic we can source & obtain them. Stellar! Also the pages are of beautiful quality paper, which is important to me when flipping thru selecting recipes. This Cookbook has made it to my Special Gift Giving List.

reviews.title: Great book by a great reporter.
reviews.body: Great book by a great reporter.I always enjoyed her work in the New York Times.

reviews.body: I loved this series.

reviews.title: Beautiful coloring book.
reviews.body: My daughter loves to color and often asks me to join her.  Instead of us both trying to color in one of her books together, I thought I'd get one of my own.  I looked at several books before deciding on this one.  I love this book and am very happy I ended up choosing it.  The book has a removable cover and underneath you can color the actual brown cover page.  The pictures are beautiful and the author/creator starts with a little intro about the world of Cocot that she created in this book.  There are various types of pages that I am looking forward to coloring.  This is a really beautiful book and if you are on the fence about it, check out some of the YouTube videos people have put up coloring the pages of this book.  I saw that she is coming out with a second book later this year and I suspect I will be ordering it when it comes out.

reviews.title: Best beginner book.  Been looking for something like this for a long time.
reviews.body: Looked online for years for something like this.  It's the best I've seen.

reviews.title: Ages 10 to 12
reviews.body:
killing animals is a personal turnoff for me, so I wish I knew that before ordering this for my 9 and 12 year olds. 12 year old Kester is a prisoner and hasn’t spoken since his mom died 6 years ago. The world is a nasty place with most animals dead and the environment no longer able to easily support human life. Kester escapes with a personal mission to save the small creatures of the earth that still survive.

The really creepy part? His father may hold the answers to the survival of Kester and the animals, he may have been the cause of all the destruction. Kester and his animal buddies set out to find him.

reviews.title: conclusion Ashes (The Seeds of America Trilogy) ... Laurie Halse Anderson
reviews.body:
A trilogy, stretching from 1776 New York City to brutal Valley Forge winter of 1777-1778 to the final battle of the American revolution at Yorktown in 1781, that should be required Middle School reading. Ashes is set in summer 1781, three years after book 2. I don't want to give any of the huge plot points away - my highest recommendation is to buy the whole trilogy for your 11 to 14 year olds.

[[ASIN:1416905855 Chains (The Seeds of America Trilogy)]] If an entire nation could seek its freedom, why not a girl? In 1776 the American Revolutionary War begins, 13 year-old Isabel wages her own fight...for freedom. Promised freedom upon the death of their owner, she and her sister, Ruth, in a cruel twist of fate become the property of a malicious New York City couple, the Locktons, who have no sympathy for the American Revolution and even less for Ruth and Isabel. When Isabel meets Curzon, a slave with ties to the Patriots, he encourages her to spy on her owners, who know details of British plans for invasion. She is reluctant at first, but when the unthinkable happens to Ruth, Isabel realizes her loyalty is available to the bidder who can provide her with freedom.  From acclaimed author Laurie Halse Anderson comes this compelling, impeccably researched novel that shows the lengths we can go to cast off our chains, both physical and spiritual.

[[ASIN:1416961453 Forge (The Seeds of America Trilogy)]] For many readers, Forge “will be one of the best novels they have ever read” (starred review from Kirkus Reviews)!  Blistering winds. Bitter cold. And the hope of a new future. In this compelling sequel to Chains, a National Book Award Finalist and winner of the Scott O’Dell Award for Historical Fiction, acclaimed author Laurie Halse Anderson shifts perspective from Isabel to Curzon and brings to the page the tale of what it takes for runaway slaves to forge their own paths in a world of obstacles—and in the midst of the American Revolution.  The Patriot Army was shaped and strengthened by the desperate circumstances of the Valley Forge winter. This is where Curzon the boy becomes Curzon the young man. In addition to the hardships of soldiering, he lives with the fear of discovery, for he is an escaped slave passing for free. And then there is Isabel, who is also at Valley Forge—against her will. She and Curzon have to sort out the tangled threads of their friendship while figuring out what stands between the two of them and true freedom.

reviews.title: Not a thriller and no redeeming characters
reviews.body: There are four women at the center of this novel. A mother running from her past, and her estranged daughter. A local woman who befriends the mother, and a lonely 90 year-old woman. None of these women have any redeeming qualities. They're all broken, and none of them learns from their past mistakes. I'm not sure why the author has such a negative attitude about women, but I definitely wasn't in the mood for this kind of in-your-face bashing, or the totally unsatisfying ending. Couldn't at least one of the women get her act together?

reviews.title: Daniel & Cass
reviews.body: This is an amazing story of how we too often lose the magic of Christmas as we move into adulthood. Despite feeling like he's invisible to his family, Daniel he is on his way to his parents' house to spend Christmas with his family. Along the way, a rude, but oh-so-gorgeous man, cuts in front of him at the checkout in the packed store, that encounter is followed by a flat tire on the deserted road to his family's house. He has no idea how to change a tire & of course, no cellphone service in the area. He doesn't know whether to cry or to scream, but suddenly, along the deserted road, comes a motorcyclist.  The biker offers help, which Daniel accepts recognizing at the same time that the biker is the super hot guy from the store. While fixing the tire, he introduces himself as Cass & during the flirtatious conversation asks Daniel what would he wish for if he were granted three wishes. To find out what Daniel's wishes are and more importantly, if they are granted, one-click now to find out if Christmas magic can make dreams come true. As always, Daryl Banner gives a HEA with no cheating.

reviews.body: It was a gift and haven't heard back if he enjoyed the book

reviews.title: I'm pretty sure i have whiplash from the twists and turns in this trilogy!
reviews.body:
I'm a huge fan of crime novels and serial killers and this book satisfied both genres wholeheartedly.

The first book reeled me in. I was interested in the Green family curse. The ending set the hook and I needed more!

The second book sealed the deal and I was shocked to read Eves involvement at the end. The blood does hold a curse that's for sure.

The third book. Blew. Me. Away. I didn't know how it could possibly hold a candle to the Green murders but wow. The Hammer in my opinion outdid the entire Green family in a fraction of the time.

Bloody. Gore filled and a mental rollercoaster.

Soooooo why end at three. Let's make it 4?! Here's to hoping the rage lives on.

reviews.title: Do you plan to Get a Dachshund? Do you Already Own a Doxie?
reviews.body:
This book is an excellent resource for anyone who is looking to purchase or rescue their first or fourth Dachshund?
Should you get an adult or puppy? And if you already own a Doxie the book gives you tips on how to work out some common problems (e.g. Housebreaking tips) with these at times demanding little Napoleons. It is a really nicely laid out book. There are lots of great photographs. My only disappointment is that they are not in color. But the author show the different sizes, the three varieties (Smooth, Wire, and Longhair), and the many different colors & combinations. The author also describes how to take care of and avoid back injuries. I have many other Dachshund books and this is among the best. It shows why these long short legged dogs with big hearts, big appetites, and big attitudes are so special. As well as, why there is a common thought that like Lay's Chips you can't just have one. I own two :0) and am thinking about acquiring a third.

reviews.title: Five Stars
reviews.body: one of the best zombie series ever.

reviews.title: Put Your Employees First and Great Results will Follow
reviews.body:
Employees First, Customers Second is an interesting management book about corporate structure and strategy. This book takes the old concept of customers first and the traditional management pyramid of command and turns both on their heads. The book preaches a new type of management gospel; one that emphasizes the importance of employees and that puts employees first, with the idea that happy employees will ultimately lead to satisfied customers.

This concept of employees first isn't a brand new idea and it has been approached by other management experts, but this particular book is the first one I have read that actually lays out a plan for putting this management philosophy into action. I like the way the author leads through the process step by step, culminating in a chapter that then stresses the need for continuous change. The book begins by stating that, in order for a change like this to work, companies must begin by making sure that employees are on board with the program. Employees need to realize that change is imperative and that everyone will benefit in the end. Some employees will resist, sometimes for good reasons (like fear of having their job eliminated) and sometimes for bad or irrational reasons (we are already profitable, so why change?). Nevertheless, it is critical that employees jump on board and realize the importance of change and this book offers some good tips that cover ways to get this message across to the workforce.

I generally like this book and its core message, and I think many companies would benefit if they put changes like those described in the book into action. However, in spite of the author's enthusiasm, I don't necessarily believe this practice would work in every type of business. The author feels otherwise, but I cannot see this management philosophy working in every situation. Thinking about past places I have worked, I cannot imagine the upper management accepting the idea of an inverted pyramid and becoming accountable to the employees. The management personnel I have known over the years have been far too arrogant to accept this type of change and would pose a potentially insurmountable obstacle to the implementation of a new philosophy such as this. The author, however, sticks to his belief that the management style he espouses will work and can be adopted by any type of company.

Management books are often boring, but to every rule there is an exception and Employees First, Customers Second is certainly an exception. This is a good management book that makes for some thought- provoking, alternative management reading and while I don't necessarily agree that the management philosophy advocated by this book will work for any company, I can appreciate the author's enthusiasm and I respect his willingness to embrace change and go against the conventional management grain.

reviews.title: Another winner from Angie Grace (and one of my favorites!)
reviews.body:
What a fun coloring book!  It has just the right combination of symmetry (mandalas, etc.) and quirky whimsy.  There is a lot of detail here, but it's not overwhelming. I've used colored pencils (Prismacolor), water-based markers (Crayola SuperTips), and alcohol-based markers (Bic Mark-Its ultra fine point and fine point), and they all work nicely.

The designs are printed on one side only, so that's a plus.  The markers do have a tendency to bleed through, however, so be sure to put a piece of paper behind the design you're coloring to prevent inadvertent bleeding onto the following page/design.  I just use a piece of paper from my printer.

I have several other Angie Grade books but I gravitate to this one and her "Balance" book -- they're about equal in terms of the level of detail. Angie was one of the "early" artists doing coloring books for adults -- her first book came out in late 2012, and there are a lot of her books available here.  Her style is instantly recognizable -- and her designs provide hours of de-stressing.

reviews.title: I Was Expecting SO Much More
reviews.body:
As an avid spinner of yarns in many different fiber combinations, I could not wait for LUXURY ONE SKEIN WONDERS to come out.  I have stashes of bamboo, soysilk, merino, silk, and alpaca fibers waiting for just the right motivation to get me to dye and spin them into balls of luxury.

I was hoping that this book would bring me such delight, but alas, it is not to be.

Contrary to the previous One-Skein Wonders book that I have been through, this book does very little to inspire me.  the patterns are indeed one skein all right, but quite frankly, if I am going to put all of that work into spinning and dyeing them to prepare for a lovely project, I sure want it to be something that looks rich and valuable and something I am going to treasure.  Something unique.

I have been through this book over and over again looking for SOMETHING that motivates me and I just can't find it.  There are a lot of gloves, mittens, baby hats (LOTS of them), baby coats, collars, pillows, placemat, purse, and other sundry boring patterns in this book.

But honestly, they are just plain boring to me.  The patterns look like anything you can download for free on the internet- or even design on your own.  There is nothing invigorating or exciting about it.

Also, the first 50 pages are set up with color photos of the projects, but the directions lack photos or drawings in most of them.  They are printed with dark sage green and a charcoal gray ink on white pages, which is nice, I guess, but the contrast is lighter than I would like making it a bit harder to read than if it was BLACK ink on white pages.

The directions are okay, and laid out well, but honestly, the lack of photos or drawings in most of them makes it confusing for me to make them.  I wish they would put the photos with the directions- but then again, I am so bored with these patterns that I guess it does not matter that much to me.

There are a few things that midly interest me, but again, like I said, with the high price of these luxury fibers, when I make something I want it to be UNIQUE and WORTH the effort and price.  Something special.  These just look rather mundane to me.

But perhaps some people will really enjoy the simplicity and blandness of the patterns.  And if you want to make something really special and expensive for babies, this is a good book to look through.  There is a lot to choose from.

reviews.title: Will be fun and easy
reviews.body: Just received this.  I can hardly wait to make them for presents.  Will be fun and easy.

reviews.title: Beautiful Prayer-Centric Devotional
reviews.body:
I selected this devotional as a gift for my wife who loves to read and has an appetite for devotionals like this one. I wasn't completely sure what to expect but [rightly] assumed it would be a good one. So far I am pleased with it.

I will start with the physical volume itself. This is an absolutely beautiful book.
The cover is gray with gold lettering, and the material used for the cover has a feel that is reminiscent of suede though it is something else. The binding is tight and there is no gap between the spine and the pages which is good. There is a single ribbon marker too which is a nice touch.

The format is a little different than that which I usually see in devotionals, though this isn't a bad thing. Normally, devotionals start with a scripture verse, then have a brief discussion, followed by a short prayer text to get the reader going. Instead, this devotional has a large prayer block, followed by one or more versus from Scripture. There's nothing at all wrong with this, it's just different than most.

Every devotion is a single page, and there is room (about 3") for writing next to each.

One feature I particularly like is that the author selects verses from different translations, rather than relying on a single translated version for everything. I really like this, as often a verse that is a little unclear in one translation can be crystal-clear in another or is worded in such a way as to be more expressive.

This is a very nice devotional that is different than others I have seen, in good ways. It is more prayer-centric than message-based and it quotes Scripture from a variety of translations. It's a beautiful volume too. This is a very nice journaling devotional that makes a superb gift.

reviews.title: Book 4 in the Shaken series
reviews.body: Love this series, the main characters, the author's humor, the southern california setting, the family and the BMWs. Anna has my heart, she is a saint, Lily still has some maturing to do, Andy is still at a fabulous young age and still adorable, Kim (Anna's sister) is still probably my favorite character after Anna and Andy. What really makes this series a super success is the chemistry between Anna and Lily, it just feel very real. And the humor wraps the story in a big bow. I get a smile just thinking of the novel. I love how the author had Anna handle the 2008 financial crash and prolonged depression with humanity and didn't create a fantasy world. Superb. If you can, read the whole series in order, you will get so much enjoyment getting the big picture.

reviews.title: Interesting But Flawed Opening Book in Alaska Series
reviews.body:
(I can't give this a 3 1/2, which is what I would really rate it.)

Charlotte Brody has left the stifling society of 1919 Yonkers behind her to join her brother Michael in Cordova, Alaska, America's "last frontier," where he is practicing medicine. A suffragette and journalist, Charlotte hopes to get a new start as well as write some provacative prose for "The Modern Woman's Review." As soon as she arrives in town, though, she discovers that not only has her brother been harboring a secret, but that human nature is not very different in this small town: soon a brutal murder occurs.

I am on the fence about this book, but realize I will probably buy the next one. I still like the characters, and a "modern girl" in still-frontier Alaska is very appealing. The rough-and-tumble of an Alaskan town post-WWI is well described. Trouble is, Charlotte is almost too headstrong. She wears her heart (and her suspicions) on her sleeve and deliberately endangers herself and others in the process. For someone who has been working for a while as a reporter, she is regrettably blunt and has no "reporter savvy." Plus big portions of the mystery are practically broadcast. When a certain event happens, for instance, you immediately realize Charlotte's other reason for coming to Cordova. The culprit is pretty obvious as the plot jogs along, and the romantic storyline developed way too quickly for my taste.

My biggest irritation with this book is the modernisms that creep into the narrative. "Pants"? "Lifestyle"? And in the preview of the sequel, a referral to an "op-ed" piece? Really? Plus some of the dialog is clunky; when Michael and Charlotte have a heart-to-heart near the end, lines include "I think we've learned valuable lessons here" and "We can help each other find peace now." Oh, good grief. I don't expect this to be written with quaint postwar prose, but the modern vocabulary really tosses one out of the story.

But...Alaska. Female journalist. One who opposes the Volstead Act to boot. I'll buy the next, but I hope Pegau tightens up her writing. Please?

reviews.title: Coming to the Country
reviews.body: This is an extraordinary book. In 1929, Merrick quit his rat-race advertising job and moved to the wilds of Labrador, where he met and married his wife Kay, a mission nurse. This volume chronicles the Merricks' winter odyssey accompanying a friend running his trapline. They experience cold, loneliness, and exhaustion, and Merrick both suffers a gunshot wound and a severely cut toe, yet both find beauty, awe and inner peace in the freedom of the wintry world. While Merrick is unflinching in describing their hardships, his prose makes the winter world poetic and majestic, and the men and women who endure and triumph over it like epic heroes of old who are still down-to-earth. For anyone who's ever wanted to break away from the humdrum. Note: this was written in 1930, and some descriptions of the Native tribes are no longer "PC." However, Merrick is much more admiring of their lifestyle than others of his era.

reviews.title: Scaled-Down, Affordable Edition of Beautiful Book on Tiffany Lamps
reviews.body:
When [[ASIN:0865651639 The Lamps of Louis Comfort Tiffany]] was first published in 2005, I very much wanted a copy, but balked at the publisher's $75 retail price.  Imagine my delight when I learned that the publisher had reissued THE LAMPS OF LOUIS COMFORT TIFFANY in this smaller-format hardcover edition at a much more affordable $35 retail price! (Both editions are available for less than full retail price on Amazon.) This smaller-format edition of the book is 10.4" x 8.7" x 1" and weighs 3 lbs.--in contrast to the original edition, which is 12.3" x 10.1" x 1.1" inches and weighs 4.2 lbs.

The photographs in this smaller-format book are gorgeous, and I doubt that either the photos or the text have suffered much, if at all, from the downsizing.  In fact, the less-hefty book is much easier to handle, if you're interested in actually reading the text, or in studying the lamp photographs closely.

What I like most about this book is that it shows the complete lamps:  the lamps have both the Tiffany glass shades (e.g., Wisteria, Daffodil, Cobweb, Dragonfly) and the elaborate, organic, metal bases that Tiffany created to perfectly complement the shades. I also love the close-ups of portions of the shades, which reveal the qualities of the individual glass pieces that went into the shades.  And I enjoy inspecting the various photos of the Tiffany workshops, the Tiffany craftspeople, and Tiffany's homes.

The book includes three background articles:  "Tiffany's Studies of Lighting" by Martin Eidelberg; "Nature Is Always Beautiful" by Martin Eidelberg; "An Alliance of Arts and Crafts: Creating a Tiffany Leaded Shade" by Martin Eidelberg and Alice Cooney Frelinghuysen.  However, the bulk of the book consists of a photo gallery of beautiful Tiffany lamps, with each lamp discussed in scholarly but readable commentary: "Important Lamps by Louis Comfort Tiffany:  Lamps selected by Nancy A. McClelland and Lars Rachen, Commentary by Martin Eidelberg.

reviews.title: Unexpected Loss Changes Everyone it Touches 🌲
reviews.body:
When a family quartet becomes a trio, everyone must assume new roles and identities, and for a young girl named Lila, that also means finding herself again. When the pain and shock of losing her father right before her 16th birthday disrupts the world she used to know, her well-meaning school counselor suggests she agree to an eight-week stay at the infamous Camp Bonaventure, a grief camp for adolescent sufferers. Despite her reluctance to go, the camp at least offers her a respite away from BOGO coffin deals and a freshly broken family tree, and while there, she experiences an unexpected attraction and all of the nervous flirtation that comes with it. Readers watch her navigate the inevitable ups and downs of finding her new path through life, and they also get to enjoy all of the teenage angst, confusion, lust, and jealousy that goes along with it!

There will always be unanswered questions that linger amidst the tangible reminders of a loved one’s former presence, but finding concealed notes often helps bring about some much-needed closure. Some choices bring with them an irreversible finality, and anyone who has ever been directly affected by suicide will relate to many of the emotions and scenes in this book. There are included mentions of eating disorders, substance abuse, marital infidelity, behavioral addictions, and murder, but I think this story would be appropriate for any teenage reader in search of a memorable coming-of-age novel.

I loved the silhouetted forest illustrations that appeared along the bottom edge of each new chapter page, and the font choices and overall length felt approachable and age-appropriate. I’d recommend this bildungsroman without hesitation!

reviews.title: No One Will Know You Used Leftovers!
reviews.body:
Partial skeins and balls, left over from larger projects, are the bane of every knitter's existence.  The yarn is too good to throw out, but there's not enough to actually make anything.  However, this book solves the problem, with its many patterns for projects so well designed that, as author Melissa Leapman says, "no one will ever know these projects were made from leftovers!"

The attractive projects include (1) a charted "jigsaw puzzle piece" baby blanket; (2) geometrically-patterned bangle bracelets; (3) striped mittens, scarves, shawls, throws, and sweaters; (4) striped and patterned shopping, sample, and tote bags; (5) a Fair Isle yoked sweater and a Fair Isle vest; and (6) many single-color hats.  The projects are grouped in the book according to the yarn weights used:  fine, lightweight, worsted, or chunky.

What I really like about this book is the lengthy introduction that discusses sorting yarns leftovers by weight and color, to ensure the best possible combinations for successful knitted fabrics.  Several pages, illustrated with color wheels, explain the scientific theory of color--including how to get good results from monochromatic color combinations, and from combinations of 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 colors.  The book also includes explanations of how to join yarns together using standard knitting techniques, or using the "Russian join" (which uses a tapestry needle).  There is a nice discussion of how to put together a "Magic Ball" of short lengths of leftover yarns of different colors and textures (the ball is knitted up like regular yarn); as well as some discussion of yarn storage.

Nearly all of the projects are fairly easy to knit.  (The Fair Isle garments, the intarsia sample bag, and the charted puzzle-piece blanket will require moderate knitting experience).  Note, though, that whether you will have enough yarn already on hand to knit many of the larger projects will depend entirely on the actual size and makeup of your personal yarn stash!  For me, this book rates an unqualified 5 stars.

reviews.title: One of the top books on project estimating I've read
reviews.body:
At 136 pages this book covers a wide array of important topics and techniques in depth. The main value of the approach the author provides is that it's both effective and consistent with best practices in project estimating.
In particular, the deliverables-based work breakdown structure approach that forms the foundation of the estimating process is one that I've been using for over a decade, and is the only sane basis, in my opinion, for establishing estimating relationships between what the project is supposed to produce, and what it takes to produce it.
I'm continually surprised by the large number of project managers, including PMPs, who don't use deliverables-based WBS.  I'm not surprised, however, by the wide disparity between estimates and actuals when this method is not used.  For this reason alone the book is invaluable, but there is even more that makes this book essential to any project manager.  For example, the resource breakdown structure approach (also known as the organizational breakdown structure), and how it relates to the WBS is not only essential to accurate project planning and estimating, but is also an integral part of earned value project management (now a part of the PMI PMBOK).  I especially liked the chapter on estimating models, which will provide project managers with proven tools and techniques, and the chapter on external projects.
Overall, this book should be on the desk of every project manager during the planning and estimating phase, and carefully followed.  I also recommend using this book with Earned Value Project Management, 2nd Edition by Quentin W. Fleming and Joel M. Koppelman.

reviews.title: Government  Abuse of Power
reviews.body:
James Bovard explains, point blank, how the United States government has grown into an uncontrollable monster, negatively impacting each and every one of us, and taking away many basic rights that were once taken for  granted.
 There is no denying that power corrupts. Give a politician the  authority to pass one oppressive law and, eventually, more and more  oppressive laws will follow. Government has become increasingly intrusive,  unethical, and dishonest over the years as more and more special interest  legislation has made its way through congress.
 This process did not take  place overnight and it will not be eliminated overnight. Americans must  work for change first on the local level, leading up to the state and  national levels. We must act quickly before it is too late. I hope that  many people will read this book and take action. A totalitarian United  States government is closer than we think.

reviews.title: One Woman's Williamsburg
reviews.body:
This short but delightful book is Bailey's love letter to Colonial Williamsburg. A self-professed history geek and science fan, Bailey has been going to "CW," as she calls it throughout the book, since she was a small child, vividly recalling in the first chapter the day in 1965 she, aged ten, and her older sister were left alone to explore the colonial area while her parents were at the pottery shop. (Yes, back in the 60s it was perfectly safe to do this if your kids followed the rules and knew to run for help if accosted by strangers—do I envy her!)

In subsequent chapters she talks about different trips, some with her family (one year they stayed at one of the Williamsburg houses) and later with her husband. As she got older, she enjoyed doing things she would have eschewed as a child: going to the art galleries, or taking time out to relax at a spa. She takes us from the Governor's Palace to the House of Burgesses to the different restaurants and into the various homes and shops, and, in one chapter, talks about how the methods of restoring the buildings and cataloging the artifacts have changed from the 1930s to modern times (in the 1930s they were strictly interested in restoring the businesses and threw the artifacts away!).

I'm not sure if anyone else but those interested in historical recreations, colonial history, or specifically Colonial Williamsburg itself would really be a fan of this book, but if any one of these categories are intriguing to you, you will probably enjoy this memoir. Keep in mind it's not a guidebook, or a be-all end-all reference to Williamsburg, but one woman's personal affection for a magical place in her childhood that continued to provide her with special memories for the rest of her life.

At the end of the book Bailey provides suggested things to see in CW as well as a bibliography of books about the restored area.

This brought was a good purchase for my intended use: as a lightweight, comfortable stretch cotton bra to wear at home during the hot months of summer.

I ordinarily wear a 36B, but, based on the reviews, I purchased this bra in a size 40 --  which was absolutely the right move, particularly after the bra shrinks in the laundry.  GO UP TWO SIZES if you are using this as a casual comfort bra or as a sleep bra. (Those who have used it  as a post breast surgery bra advise going up three sizes.)

Some reviewers have commented that the bottom of the front closure is rough in a certain place that is uncomfortable. My bra does not have this problem, but it came with a label that said something like "new comfort redesign."

Some have commented that sometimes the hooks in front pop open in the middle section. This is not true of my bra, but if it did happen, it's a simple matter to tighten bra hooks a bit with a pair of pliers.

Keep in mind if you decide to purchase this bra that you are paying for a very inexpensive Fruit of the Loom product. Some of the reviews criticize this bra in a way that might be more appropriate if they had paid for a high-end product.  In my opinion, the ratio of cost to value is very good, and that is the only fair way to judge a product.

 Here's what this bra will NOT do:

 Prevent bouncing during sports activities.

 Obscure pointy nipples through a thin top.

 Provide strong support to large breasts.

reviews.title: His New Fave Sweats...
reviews.body: I have a confession to make. I was looking for a specific name brand of men's sweatpants on Amazon for my husband and couldn't find what I was looking for, so I began to look at other brand name sweatpants.  By the time I came across these Hanes Men's EcoSmart fleece sweatpants, I was tired of looking and just wanted to be finished. So I chose the color and size and placed my order.  He wasn't overly thrilled when I informed him I couldn't get the brand he wanted.  That changed when the Hanes sweatpants I ordered arrived.  First, the sweatpants arrived days EARLIER than expected, which was an awesome surprise!  I took them out of the package and was immediately impressed. This is not a pair of thin, cheap sweatpants, even though the price is incredibly low.  They're VERY well made with nice, even stitching.  The material is nice and soft.  The drawstring is easy to use, the elastic at the bottom of the legs is comfortable and doesn't make marks in skin. I ordered his normal size and they are a perfect fit.  I washed the sweatpants prior to him wearing for the first time. They washed and dried beautifully.  In the end, the sweatpants he wasn't overly thrilled about because they weren't the brand he wanted are now his FAVORITE sweatpants! Hanes EcoSmart sweats are of excellent quality, they wash and wear well and they're incredibly comfortable. Definitely recommended! (And now, I need to end this review so I can order a pair of Hanes EcoSmart women's sweats for ME!!!! lol)

reviews.title: Great for travel ...
reviews.body:
I first purchased a similar top by Esenchel in a long-sleeved version and liked it so much that I decided to get this short-sleeved edition for a major trip earlier this year (a 131-day around-the-world cruise).

The style is ideal -- it's great for casual wear, but you can also dress it up with a scarf or jewelry.  I brought a bunch of multi-color scarves to coordinate six of these Esenchel tops I had purchased to wear for dinners in the Compass Rose dining room.  They were wonderful!

The fabric is soft and not too heavy -- the first part of the cruise included Hawaii and the South Pacific where the temps and humidity were often uncomfortable.  The fit of this top isn't too "snug," which was great for the weather.  It fits nicely across the shoulders and bust but then widens to a looser fit down to the hem.  I'm a "larger" person (I believe "Juno-esque" is the term), and the cut of this top does a great job of accentuating the positives while minimizing the negatives.

I used the ship's laundry service with instructions to wash in warm water and tumble dry on "delicate" -- and they came out perfect every time.

Although the trip was cut short after only 53 days due to the coronavirus outbreak, I still managed to wear and wash all 6 tops at least twice and they held up just fine.  Easy to pack (they don't take up a lot of space), and what few wrinkles appear usually disappear after hanging for a couple of hours.

I'll definitely purchase this brand again -- I'm going to need a few more of the long-sleeved version for a trip above the Arctic Circle planned for next year ... !

reviews.title: Skechers Cankton WORK Steel Toe Relaxed Fit Shoes 77055/BKCC - PERFECT & COMFORTABLE
reviews.body: I have never had a pair of Steel Toes I didn't hate. I still used them and wore out those I had before I finally bought a Suzuki Boulevard C50T Cruiser motorcycle a couple weeks ago. I wanted a tough sole shoe with a steel toe, especially while I get used to stopping and restarting the bike, but I wanted the shoe to have some feel for the gears and brakes. These Skechers Cankton WORK steel toes were as comfortable as my nicest and most expensive Adidas, New Balance or Reebok tennis shoes, or as any of my street shoes.  (I did take out the Skechers insole (only because as a WORK shoe it put more padding under my heel than I needed for riding.)  I put in my own favorite brand of insoles for tennis - more arch support, and a little less heel and toe support - and the shoes felt even better.  I had a lot more sensitivity to the left foot platform gear shifter, and to the right foot brake on my Cruiser.  I would not wear these for tennis, but with these I no longer have to pick my oldest or dirtiest tennis shoes, just to go for a walk in the woods, or in the park after it's rained.  I go for rides, I since I don't notice the steel toe at all, I even wear them just to run errands.  I normally wear a 10.5 M, but I bought these in a 10 W and they fit great.

reviews.body:
I purchased the 'Left/Right Brain" design.  This is my second hardshell case from this company for my MacBook Pro.  The first one was a faux wood look and was great quality.  One day it took a tiny 'crash' into a bookshelf.  It did the job it was intended to do, protected my computer, but got cracked up on the edge of the shell.  I liken this to a bike helmet- when it does it's job properly, you will need to replace it after the fall, I digress.  This case is from the same company, but this one shows my Mac apple while the computer is closed but on. reviews.title: Too High Maintence For Me To Bother With
reviews.body:
The need for an uninterruptible power source is obvious to anyone with a computer or other expensive electronic equipment. The very day this product arrived, before I even opened the box, a severe thunderstorm knocked out power in my neighborhood. My two computers immediately went down and the screen on one kept flashing on and off even after all the power was dead. So yes, a UPS seems like an important piece of equipment these days. Sadly, this one is not for me. To be fair to the manufacturer though I need to give you a bit of context to help you evaluate if my reaction and this review would be applicable to you or not.

At age 70 I have a pretty low tolerance for muss and fuss. If it requires special handling, if it is a hassle to use, I don't want it. If it's not plug and play, I won't bother with it. For example, I do all my laundry in one load throwing everything in together without any sorting of any kind. It all gets washed and dried on the hot cycle. Anything that can't handle that gets tossed out. I treat everything like that. This UPS looks like an industrial strength product but acts like a delicate little snowflake. Coming out of the box it has 20 pages of instructions they want you to read before using. I didn't bother, just plugged it in, turned it on, and starting using the USB charger to juice up a battery run children's night light. A little while later I noticed a burnt plastic smell and saw the warping on the case that you can see in the attached photos. So this thing is not for me. More detail oriented and careful folks might have better luck with it.  Thus I'm giving it a neutral 3 star rating and suggest you read through all the reviews here before deciding whether you want to try it yourself or not.

reviews.title: BUYER BEWARE!
reviews.body:
My unit worked just fine for the first few months, then the battery failed and within a short time of the battery failing, the entire unit did not provide any power.  As it comes with a 3-year warranty, I tried to got through the normal Amazon return procedures and it says "For safety reasons, items that are classified as hazardous materials or use flammable liquids or gases cannot be returned to Amazon.com. Customers should dispose of hazardous materials according to Local, State and Federal regulations. Customers should contact their local government or local waste company for directions on how to dispose of Household Hazardous Waste."

I may still be able to get a refund through the manufacturer, but bear in mind that Amazon.com does not provide any survive for this item, so BUYER BEWARE!

reviews.title: Works for me.
reviews.body:
Before this stand, I used another Fellowes one for my laptop at home, and it proved its worth--for a while. However, with my new desk setup, I needed something which I could use while changing the height and angle of my laptop screen in a way the old stand simply couldn't. I have a Unicomp keyboard and Logitech mouse which I prefer using, and my "home" laptop needed a better stand.
Enter this Lift.

I've seen many angled laptop stands, and that's what I had in mind when I wanted to switch my old one out. Plus, my old one was better suited for the monitor at work, so I wanted to take that when I had the chance. Finally, I had the opportunity to get an angled one, so I jumped on it.

I'm not using this stand with my laptop by itself. I'm using it as a supplemental to "lift" it up with my home desktop setup being my keyboard and mouse. For that, the stand works marvelously. The angle and height are just about right; I no longer have to arch my neck uncomfortably forward. Plus, I can take my old stand to work and finally have proper posture there too.
I can't see using this by itself. My hands would quickly become painfully uncomfortable. Heck, I can't stand using keyboards with their built-in mini stands. I honestly don't know why they're there; the angle cramps my wrists very fast.

So for my use, I think the stand is great. There's even some empty real estate near the back to put things under, and it seems sturdy enough overall. It's currently holding my Toshiba 17" Windows PC, which is snugly fit.

reviews.title: Packs a punch!
reviews.body: I ordered the 'DOSS SoundBox Pro+ Wireless Bluetooth Speaker with 24W Impressive Sound, Booming Bass, Wireless Stereo Pairing, Mixed Colors Lights, IPX5 Waterproof, 15 Hrs Battery Life, 66 ft Bluetooth Range -Grey' for my oldest daughter as she keeps "borrowing" my wireless Bluetooth speaker and rarely gets it back to me. When I first received the device and opened it, I had my doubts that this one would compare to my device however I was pleasantly surprised. The sound quality for this little guy is amazing and at 24W gets fairly loud. The Bass boost button ads just a touch more Bass but not as much as I would expect but again, for how small this is, it packs a punch. The lighting inside the front grill is fun and ads to the "fun factor". At first my daughter was not so impressed with the speaker, but after using it now for a while, she stated that she loves the grey color, the light effects and the sound quality. Also a nice little surprise with this speaker is that you can ad music to your own SD card (up to 32GB) and install it directly into, and play it through the unit. Though I don't think my daughter will use this feature, it's nice that DOSS included the option. Overall this was a win for both myself and my daughter.

reviews.title: Exceeded my expectations with clean balanced sound and undistorted bass.
reviews.body:
[[VIDEOID:4c60e87ead4c44abcba14a2d6daa5b1e]] When I test speakers I play the type of music that is meant for headphones because of the meticulous care taken when mixing the recordings. I don't expect headphone quality, but I do expect balanced sound and on occasion, a little extra "undistorted" bass. I do like my bass and the Doss Soundbox Pro+ did not disappoint.  The bass was punchy and clean without being overwhelming.
Not only did this fill my living room with clear, undistorted sound, but I could hear it two rooms away without it sounding too bright or boomy at max volume. I am not sure if this would be loud enough to blast through a large room filled with noisy people, but it's perfect for smaller gatherings and apartments that share common walls with neighbors.
I mostly use this with my computer, so the even though the lights are fun, they're a bit distracting near my screen, and I was able to turn it off by holding the "extra bass" button for a few seconds.  This speaker paired quickly with all of my devices, and the sound quality exceeded my expectations, I highly recommend it.

The noise alone will deter any further intrusion from a a would be burglar, and it will definitely alert you to some one opening that window or even that door that you might want to chime.  They are battery operated so I set an reminder on my phone to check them once a year since I won’t be opening these particular windows all that much. The TV plug was at the opposite end of the TV, from my cables.  I added a second set. The wall mount prevented me from sliding the cover down, and the floor stopped me from sliding it up.  Cutting was an option.  Instead, I placed the plug cord in the holder with screw holes, placed the cover over it, and then pressed the cover into the holder until it snapped in. The same way you snap a lid on a refrigerator bowl.  Worked fine.  Using a second set for just one plug may seem like overkill, but it really balances the setup, and looks great.

reviews.title: Good for Securing Your Home
reviews.body:
Most of the places I have lived have been reasonably safe, so I have never felt any pressing need to add a camera security system to my home. I already have an alarm system, which is useful, but no camera system. I decided that it would be good to be able to see people at the main entrances to my home/property and this convinced me to add the Arlo Ultra - 4K UHD Wire-Free Security 2 Camera System to my house.

Setting this security system up is simple enough. You have to mount the included 2 cameras and it doesn’t take much time to complete this step. I placed one of them by my front door and the other one just outside my garage, facing the driveway. The gated entrance to my backyard is right there, and I usually leave my car in the driveway and not the garage, so this seemed like a good place.

There are many things to like about this security camera system, like the wide angle of view that is good for seeing from my backyard gate to the end of my driveway. You can even speak back and forth with someone at your front door and this can prove useful when you want to avoid talking directly, face to face, with solicitors.

With the image quality, although it isn’t as sharp as I expected, it seems sufficient to me. I haven’t experienced any intruders thus far- knock on wood- so I haven’t necessarily needed to get crystal clear details. One limitation I have is that I haven’t owned a camera security system before. This is a first for me, so I don’t have any point of comparison. Still, the picture quality seems good. And I like the notification system. Any motion detection is set up to record, so you can see what is going on and you know quickly.

The app itself is user- friendly enough but one thing to keep in mind is that the Arlo Smart Servive and cloud recording are free for only the first year. After that, you have to pay for a subscription. I will wait to see if the system is worth my while, then decide whether to subscribe. A year of free usage time should be sufficient to make the call.

Security is important and the Arlo Ultra - 4K UHD Wire-Free Security 2 Camera System is a good way to keep safe. Two cameras are definitely better than one because I am able to secure the two areas of my property where an unwanted individual is most likely to show up. I find the app and picture quality good and the system as a whole has enough positive points to recommend.

reviews.title: Good music player with streaming apps. Sort of Android, but not necessarily what you think
reviews.body:
Yes, the UI and apps are very clearly Android. No, it isn't a mini tablet.
Players like this are an interesting market that is hard to pin the audience down for. There are music players that are cheap on the market for those that would rather have a dedicated player (ie, not their phone). However the user interface tends to be wonky and slow, and newer generation features like bluetooth 5+ and streaming are often a mixed bag, if even available.
The idea behind players like this one, is that it is based on a supported operating system (Android, in this case) so it can play almost any format you throw at it, has plenty of support for popular streaming apps and features, as well as a familiar user interface that is already so polished, it seems silly to reinvent the wheel like the super cheap older media players.
Is it a mini tablet or phone without service? Not exactly. This is not a Google certified device, it does not have the play store or any Google apps on it. Unlike some other Android based players, I couldn't even get sideloaded apk files to install (it kept throwing errors at me). It seems like this device was purposely locked down to keep it an mp3 player. That's good in some ways, my kids aren't allowed unlimited screen time and their schools don't want them bringing smartphones around, so this is a strictly music-player oriented device (especially once you remove things like the browser for them, which it allows you to do). But I also know there are more capable players out there, some of which have quad DAC audio chips. Also, what happens when an app gets updated and goes out-of-date? Sometimes streaming services make changes and updated clients are required for it to work, however you are largely stuck with the version that this came with unless they issue a firmware update or something.
This is still cheaper than the higher end mp3 players that support high end DAC and app updates, but not by much. It seems to be a sort of in-between product. If you have a use for something like this, it could be a pretty good option. But if you're expecting a handheld tablet or alternative concept to an ipod touch, it is not exactly that.

The lens will separate from the mount if any hit is taken by the lens and that in-turn tears the flex cables, making a repair an expensive proposition. reviews.title: HDMI - Highly Disappointing Misrepresented Item? You be the judge...
reviews.body:
When researching HDMI cables I chose this one specifically because of the claims that it was heavy duty and made to last.  My experience has shown that to absolutely not be the case.

I had this 40’ HDMI Cable plugged in to my TV. When I initially ran the cable I took great care to ensure there would never be strain from tension on either HDMI plug by zip tying in several places prior to where the cord terminated at either end.

The only strain on the plug that failed was literally GRAVITY - I had the cord loose behind hanging behind the TV to where it met with my other cables where it was zip tied.

I have NEVER unplugged this HDMI plug so this is not an issue concerning wear and tear.

Due to our TV having a multitude of HDMI ports it is not necessary to plug and unplug cables, but several devices rarely get used.  I discovered this HDMI plug failure after not using for quite some time.  I was shocked to find that the plug had in fact bent out and down due to gravity!

If purchasing from e Dragon expect nothing in the way of customer support other than the absolute bare minimum required.

This is absolutely not a product I would recommend.  Very disappointing.

I bought this before Thanksgiving to replace my old Teflon-coated turkey-roasting pan and rack. I have become concerned about the safety of using Teflon products at high temperatures, and I use a fast, high heat roasting method for turkey, So I decided that it was time to move on to uncoated stainless steel.

This product performed perfectly, both at the roasting stage and at the gravy-making stage. I expected it to be very difficult to clean, but I was pleasantly surprised that it came out sparkling after a relatively short warm, soapy soak and moderate scrubbing. Both the pan and the rack are heavy and strong. I'm delighted with my purchase.

reviews.title: Easy to set up.
reviews.body:
Words cannot express how excited I was to get this bed. A year ago we got our first memory foam mattress and I was over the moon (or under, since I was happily sleeping in its light). But when we were getting a *king*-size bed, I was never happier.
I thought this was the same brand as one we had set up last year, but it was not. I also set up one by this brand earlier this week, but all in all the three platform beds I've assembled have been the same. The shipping box comes with the headboard and everything else inside. It was a bit of a pain hauling it up three flights of stairs to our apartment, but we pulled through! I was afraid when opening it because some parts of the box had been torn through, but thankfully there weren't any rips or anything.

Everything you need to assemble the bed is included. You really need only one hex wrench (I forget the exact size); it comes with one, but I used my own anyway. There are a few spare screws, but nothing else is spared. I'm not sure who makes this bed; the included instruction sheet had Modern Essentials instead of Zinus, so Zinus could very well just be the supplier. Dunno.

Anyway, once everything was set up we were good to go. I assembled it by myself in about an hour. The only complaint I have, however, is that, like the same platform bed we have but without the headboard, this bed's center peg doesn't sit on the floor all the way. There's about a centimeter gap or so. When you lie on it it obviously goes down and touches the floor, but with...um...certain movement...you're going to have that center bed bang on the floor repeatedly. Hopefully you don't have neighbors right under your bedroom!

The headboard isn't very high, but it's fine for us since we stash stuff on top, like phones or water bottles, and that makes them more easily accessible.

Besides that uneven center peg, it's a great bed so far, and is very easy to assemble.

reviews.title: Storage space we could use for her "craft projects" After getting this platform bed frame 2 days ago I am more than pleased with
reviews.body:
I ordered this bed frame because of few reasons.

1. I haven't had a bred frame in 10 years.
2. My fiancé wanted to stop sleep on a bed sitting on the ground
3. Storage space we could use for her "craft projects"

After getting this platform bed frame 2 days ago I am more than pleased with this product. I found not needing a box spring amazing because for the price of box springs now I could just buy this sleek product. I am amazed that everything can fit inside the headboard when we moved in about 6 months. After sitting out all the pieces it took about 10 mins to put together and most of that was just making sure all the bolts were tight. I saw some people complain about oh its only 6 inches of space not 7, well honestly the slim boxes you can by from any store fit perfectly under the frame. We have 2 dogs that love getting under the beds and the fact that its short they aren't able to get under easy when the boxes are in use.

I am very satisfied with this purchase and would recommend this bed frame to anyone.
