They loved this unicorn. It was so cute. They just loved that it had the babies with it.

This is a very adorable stuffed animal. My daughters really enjoy them, and they liked her a lot. This is a good size for us.
I am pleased with the quality of the doll. My kids had no problems with her. She held up well to their handling. We have many items from this company and have been very happy with them.
This would also make a very nice gift. My girls like getting dolls the best of all.
She looks just like the picture. I think the price was fair. I would recommend it.

reviews.title: Cute mommy unicorn
reviews.body:
The PixieCrush Stuffed Mommy Unicorn is very cute in person. The unicorn’s fur is soft, though the mane and tail are a bit limp. The tails on all the unicorns are flat, like two pieces of fun fur sewn together.

Kids won’t need any help putting the babies inside the mommy unicorn or taking them out. They fit without needing to really stuff them inside. The mommy unicorn is snuggable even when the babies are out; she doesn’t feel skinny or limp. The pull for the zipper is made of metal, the zipper itself is plastic.

Construction on everyone is pretty good. I didn’t see any loose threads or stitches, missing fur, or other issues. The inside of the mommy unicorn’s stomach is lined with a durable mesh to keep her stuffing from coming out.

The unicorns are made in China. I didn’t notice any smells when removed from the packaging. The unicorn arrives in a plastic bag, with the babies already inside.

reviews.title: Super cute!
reviews.body: Could be my pregnancy hormones, but I didn’t want to give this up to my niece for Christmas. I did, don’t worry, I’m not a horrible person! It’s sooooo cute and she loved it!

reviews.title: A decent value
reviews.body:
Kinda cheesey.  The bottles Ave very light weight and tip over easy..... Add that to the fact the sand settles by the next day, so your left with a bunch of mixed colors at the top.
Kids didn't care though. They still enjoyed it!

reviews.title: Lots of fun for my 8 and 5 year olds
reviews.body: My 5 year old son and 8 year old daughter had a great time filling the containers with different colored sand. It was great to see the differences in the way each layered their sand. Great for creative minds and crafting for young children. They were so proud of their little creations!

reviews.title: The ultimate kit indeed! Could use a second funnel though
reviews.body:
My kids are four and six, and had an absolute blast doing this sand art kit. They participated together to choose which containers each of them would get to fill, then shared the funnel pretty well amongst themselves, with my six-year-old deciding ultimately that the four-year-old could have the funnel rather than try to trade it back and forth, and he could just be careful pouring the sand out of the bags.

The glitter and glow-in-the-dark sand were obviously the most popular, but the other colors were vibrant and bright and my children really liked them.

I didn't care for the stickers, but my kids love them, and the two of them made a number of pieces of "art" that they were able to display in their rooms, share with grandma, etc. and the whole set gave them a couple hours of joy, and then another hour of joy the next day finishing off the last couple of projects. They took a lot of pride in carefully choosing how their sand art would look.

I appreciated that the lids were easily glued on. Overall this was a really fun set and would make a great gift for a kid in the 5 to 8 age range especially.

reviews.title: It made my granddaughter very happy.
reviews.body: This was a Christmas gift for my granddaughter and she loved it. She was able to make beautiful multi layer multi color pieces with the unusual bottles in the kit. I recommend for any child.

reviews.title: snap bracelets
reviews.body: I purchased this for holiday family game and my sister who runs a preschool chose it.  She has a little friend who would really love them.  They are pretty and look like fun. She will give me a report if there are any issues that should be reported.

reviews.title: Great craft!
reviews.body: Fun craft to do with kids. Stickers last long on bracelets and a great idea to do with kids. The color of the bracelets are 2 colors so front may be silver, back will be gold! Really cool craft

reviews.title: Sparkling fun for your little one
reviews.body: This is a very small set but really cute for the price. Like every Melissa and Doug product I've owned this is just as good. It's very good quality. The kids all had fun making the bracelets. The only thing I wish was different is that the stickers stuck better. That's why I gave it 4 stars instead of 5. This isn't a huge set. It only makes 3 bracelets and it's about as thin as a folder but it's a cute add on gift or stocking stuffer. I recommend it.

reviews.title: Five Stars

reviews.body: It's too bad so many kids have attention spans than can be measured in nanoseconds.  But for those with an interest in science who can put down their cell phones long enough,, this is a great hands on way to learn some interesting simple applications of magnetiism.  And if your kids aren't fascinated by it, there's a chance your pets might.  My cat loves playing with the finished projects which take only a few mInutes each to set up.

reviews.body: I have purchased 2 of these and my grandchildren absolutely love it..  I have been using this for at least 3 years.  They make the most beautiful colored eggs.

reviews.body: I bought this so my toddler could color eggs for years to come.  I’m not sure what we did wrong, but the ink kept coming off.  My eggs were refrigerated and the condensation did not allow the ink to dry.  We tried using our own Sharpies thinking it was markers that came with the set, but no such luck. reviews.title: So much fun!

reviews.title: Fun Build
reviews.body: My kids loved the Venom mech suit and the shootable missiles in this set.  Personally, I'm on the fence of the Spidey jet build, but it is a fun set.  The boys took about 20 minutes to finish the kit and said this was a five star set. I would actually leave it at 4.5 because I really think the jet model is a little weak.  There are a number of unusual pieces in the set that will be treasured for rebuilds and I think that is where the model is headed for.  It's a pretty decent set, I just would have liked a bit strong model for the Jet.

reviews.title: Great set
reviews.body:
We really love LEGOs in this family. My son can spend hours playing with them. I really like them because he can be creative. Once he is done putting together the item he will often make his own creations.

I love the quality of the LEGOs. I don’t think we have ever had one break and we have many, many sets. I also like that he has something to play with once he makes it. Of course he has to be careful with it, but if he is, he can play with it.

These make great gifts. I think my son loves it the best of all. It is good for both boys and girls. It is also nice when the set goes with something like this one does.

This was a good set. He was able to put it together on his own. It really kept him occupied for quite a while. I think it is also educational. It is good that he can follow the directions and also for hand-eye coordination.
I would highly recommend this set.

reviews.title: Lego 76150: Marvel: Spider-Jet vs Venom Mech
reviews.body:
I’m looking at the Lego Marvel Spider-Man Spiderjet vs. Venom Mech set as an adult collector. I suspect for many AFOLs (adult fan of Lego), the reason to buy this set is for the Spider-Man Noir minifigure. This is currently the only set Spider-Man Noir is available in.

As for the builds… the Spiderjet is so blocky! While I like that the weapons launchers work, I wish they weren’t big square hunks attached to either side of the jet. Every time I look at the jet, those big blue squares are the first thing I see. It’s the most non-aerodynamic plane I’ve seen.

The Venom Mech is a bit better. It’s similar in size to the individual mech sets (Spider-Man, Thanos, and Iron Man). But I don’t like how the fingers on the hands are attached. The fingers snap off very easily, so watch out for that if you play with the mech.

reviews.title: Nice, small set
reviews.body: B, the ten year old boy, had a lot of fun putting this together. To be honest, it wasn’t very hard for him and didn’t take long, as he has a lot of experience with much larger kits, with many, many more pieces, but he had fun. It was a nice quiet rainy day activity and the set is nice. Not sure on sturdiness, but I would venture just a guess, that it isn’t terribly tough. But remains to be seen, if it proves sturdier than I think, I will update for more stars

reviews.title: Beautiful, detail-sculptured horses like the Schleich brand
reviews.body:
This 6 pack of ponies went to a 3 year old lover of all things horse. The toys are 4-6" long & around 4" tall. They aren't exactly to scale with each other but are about the same size. They vary in poses like galloping, trotting & standing. Their legs are positioned that they will all easily stand up and are relatively stable despite the long legs & high center of gravity. They arrived with their legs snapped into clear polycarbonate stands which helps preserve the leg positioning.

I don't know a lot about horses but these seem very realistic, beautifully sculpted & highly detailed. Their heft, sculpture & paint is on par with the expensive Schleich brand toy animals I used to buy when my daughter was younger.

reviews.title: Great horse figures for imaginative play!
reviews.body: We live on a farm next to a horse farm, so when the grandkids visit, the horses are always a curiosity.  Call me naive, but I thought if we have these really great horse figures, that they might actually go out in the grass and dirt, and have some pretend games with the horses.  And, that’s what they did!  No “Grandma, can I play with your  IPad?”  Just good, dirty, imaginative play.  Miracle!  I love these figures - they’re well-made, nicely detailed, and built to last!  At last, a great idea!

reviews.title: Cute
reviews.body: Cute, some are not detailed as much as others.

reviews.title: Great little starter set of horses
reviews.body:
I have both of the sets featured on this page, and really love the diversity of both. The set with the Mustang includes a more standard array of horses, while the other one has some of the unusual and differently size horses that make play a little bit more interesting.

The horses with the Mustang are an interesting set with each horse looking a little bit different. The only thing that I don't love about it is that the two white horses appeared to be from different lines entirely. One of the horses is very slick and shiny, while the other one is detailed a little bit more realistically. Why are both of these included in the same set? It looks like one should be a low-end set, and one should be in a much nicer set.

In any case though, my kids did not notice any deficiency at all, and absolutely loved incorporating the horses into their existing farm set up. This is a great set of horses for playing.

reviews.body: I bought this as gift for a two year old and was told by his parents that this toy keeps him very engaged and has become a favorite!

reviews.title: Good clean fun.
reviews.body: Rarely do I write reviews, especially positive ones, but this one deserves it. I purchased this product for my 3 year old niece so that she would have something to do at our big family Thanksgiving. She was excited as she looked forward to opening it (after 3 more bites of sweet potatoes). We unwrapped the box together as she sat on my lap. The first thing that I noticed was the multitude of colors -an almost overwhelming array- which immediately sparked creativity and imagination in both of us. She doesn't like to get messy. This is not at all the "messy" type of clay. It sticks to itself and nothing else (floor, tablecloth, hands and face). It even has a pleasant, almost cotton candy, aroma. I was so focused on the mindful, stress relieving activity of squishing and snapping the clay, I almost didn't notice the hilarity of what was happening all around the rest of the dining room table. Every member of my family, from age 3 to 66 was playing with the clay. There were enough individual packs to go around and we still have a few unopened colors to delve into next time we gather. The turkey was cooked perfectly, the butternut squash soup was delicious, and Lord knows I love that pumpkin pie; but, the real hit of the party was Sago Brothers Magic Clay.

reviews.title: Great product
reviews.body: Bought these for the grand kids. They love it!! Safe non-toxic. Many colors.

reviews.title: Great for Beginners
reviews.body: I've never been into arts or good at them, but as I like to try new things, this was suggested to me. For the value? It's pretty cool. 24 packs of soft clay to work with, generous amounts for smaller projects; has sculpting tools, and a few bonuses (little baggies, items for keychains, etc). Works well for either kids or adult beginners. Love that this kit contains what a beginner needs. It comes in a compact little box so it doesn't take up a lot of room - great for dorms or motorcoaches. The colors are bright and cheerful, so I'm very excited to use this and see what I can create.

reviews.title: Kind of cheaply made but a cool toy and fun decoration!

Plastic is slightly on the cheap side but I don't think these are that expensive so that's to be expected.

reviews.title: Boring, best for kids 6 and under
reviews.body: It gets boring fast. Kiddo aged 8 and me finally just had to stop because it doesn't take much skill to just never drop the ball into the tower. With younger kiddos who have less fine motor skills it would be a great way to work on those while getting the concepts of balancing and counterbalancing.

reviews.title: Game cheaply made
reviews.body: My 5yo Grandson loves Mario & this was on his Christmas gift list. I took everything out of the package to put the game together to see how it works to prep to play with him. It’s cheaply made & doesn’t stay in one piece very well. The red markers the characters go on don’t securely stay in place once a character is put on the red marker. Briefly but not well enough to actually get a game going. It’s not sturdy period. The actual game itself has little purpose. For a 5yo he will play with it his own way with the characters & the small ball. The characters are cute & accurate to Mario & his friends. $20 for this is overpriced. I wouldn’t suggest this if you’re looking for an actual game to play with your little one.

reviews.body: Definitely recommend this item!! My husband used it to help make a balloon archway for his parents 50th Wedding Anniversary party🎈 and it was beautiful! Easy to use and overall great product! Thank you so much!

reviews.title: Typical, expected high quality
reviews.body:
I purchased this for display on the side of my refrigerator. I cannot use the base body because it is on a wee platform to hold it upright.

That will be nice to have when we get bored with it on the fridge and I put it on my desk.

Melissa and Doug never disappoint, not once in the decades we have been buying them.

One of the outstanding toy companies of all time, right up there with Lincoln Logs, Lego, Erector sets, microscopes and all the beloved toys from childhood.  My 10 and 12 year  old grandchildren have graduated to robots, electronics, dremel sets and other adult tools, but Melissa and Doug stuff manages to surface with regularity.  We just love this stuff!

reviews.title: Great for learning layers of the human body, just keep in mind they are atomically correct.
reviews.body:
I bought this for my 4 year old daughter, she's been watching "The Magic School Bus" on Netflix and has since been really interested in the human body. She'll walk into he room and say, "Look Mom! My bones and muscles are holding me up!" She also has an older sister that has cerebral palsy, and she understands that her sisters muscles don't work like other kids. She loves being able to see all the different layers of the body.

**One thing that caught me off guard was the different boy and girl parts. The organs and skin layers have girl parts and boy parts.**

Wasn't a big deal for me, as we have always taught the atomically correct names for boys and girls private parts, and my kids understand the differences between them.
I just thought I would mention it so you know what you're getting.

reviews.title: Awesome
reviews.body: This is a wonderful learning tool for my 6 year old "wanna be" pediatrician. He's learning so much.

reviews.title: Good price good delivery
reviews.body: Christmas gift. Good price

reviews.title: Mediocre Product - temperature gauge takes on moisture, etc.
reviews.body: This product should deliver on it's core offering: temp gauge, wind vane/compass, water collector. Here's what it does.  Temp gauge is very low quality and takes on moisture so that it is unreadable.  Wind vane does not measure wind velocity. Compass works. Water collector works. 5/5 stars.  As a kids activity the assembly is a good exercise, but as a scientific piece of equipment, even for a science project, it is not.  If you live in a low moisture climate, the temp gauge will not be an issue, but in the Puget Sound on the West Coast it is.

reviews.title: Excellent Springtime Gift
reviews.body: Got this for my son’s birthday in a few weeks.  Just looking at it, this is a pretty solid all in one STEM kit.  Everything feels decent quality.  Can’t wait to get started with it!  We love these ongoing projects and this one should last for several months at least.

reviews.title: Junk Kit
reviews.body: This is the worst science/craft kit we have ever used. I opened the box and felt like I was peering into a junk drawer. You get three balloons. (Hilariously, they had the exact same balloons in a gift bag from a Memorial Day party.) Just white balloons with stars printed on them. You also get a cut off top of a water bottle for a funnel. You use the water bottle funnel to add water beads and glitter (you get a couple tiny packs) to the balloon. Add water. That’s it. The filled balloon is your Squoosh-O. They look nothing like the picture on the box. You can’t really see the beads or glitter inside the not at all clear balloons. I think you’d be better off DIYing this thing. Balloons, water beads, used water bottle. No need for the kit.

reviews.title: Soooo much fun
reviews.body: I read the reviews so I wasn’t expecting much with the balloons and some beads. I didn’t set my expectations high. My kids had a blast with this though!! They loved picking colors, and filling the balloons. Then they loved waiting for the water beads to fill up. I have three kids (5,8,11) and it was nice they each got to make one. They have really enjoyed playing with their completed squishy—they look great!! Craft took about 30 minutes and was pretty clean.

reviews.title: Fun and stress-relief for kids and their families
reviews.body: The girl is going to love this kit. She is hooked on slime so much that she makes videos on how to make it on you tube. This kit comes with everything you need to make 3 balls. You get 4 balloons, 2 packs of expanding water beads, glitter, a funnel and the instructions. I know I have had a stress ball before the dog ate it and the girl would squeeze it all the time. So I know this is going to be a hit for her. She will be making stress balls for everyone. She will love the glittery stars and galaxy from the mix of water beads and glitter. It makes it very eye-appealing to kids.

reviews.title: Very good buy...well worth it!

We have many toys from this company. They make a lot of different products and we have generally been very happy with them. It worked well.

Starshine comes with seven charms that you can place on the magic hearts and you will hear over 100 different sounds and phrases. The talking is bilingual. The horn changes color. This is an enchanting unicorn and little ones will enjoy playing with this.

reviews.title: The perfect gift for unicorns 🦄 lovers
reviews.body: My granddaughter is gonna love it. It came in perfect condition and it works fine! Thanks Amazon

reviews.title: She is so pretty and looks just like her photos!
reviews.body:
This toddler girl doll by Jizhi is so pretty! She looks exactly like her pictures. She is bigger than I expected her to be and her limbs and head are posable.

She is packaged very nicely and comes with 2 blue bows for her hair, a magnetic pacifier, bottle, birth certificate, instructions, and a bag of accessories.

Her head and limbs are soft vinyl and her body is cloth and is slightly weighted. Her hair is brown and curly and is nicely rooted. Her hair is very full.

Her vinyl is nicely painted with blushing all over to give that realistic look. She has the bluest eyes and the most adorable smile with her 2 teeth showing!

Her dress is very pretty and reminds me of Dorothy from The Wizard of Oz.

This toddler girl doll looks very realistic and I think both adult collectors and children would adore her. She is nicely detailed and well worth the price.

reviews.title: She’s so lifelike, it’s unbelievable!
reviews.body: This doll is absolutely adorable and so lifelike that it’s unbelievable! It comes packaged in this nice box and comes with a birth certificate. There is an option for a full body vinyl, and a cloth body. I ordered both, and both are amazing quality. The cloth body does come with a cute little stuffed bunny rabbit though (pictured). The quality is out of this world for the price. For a real reborn you would pay thousands of dollars for this same doll. She looks just like a real baby. So precious!

reviews.title: Hollow Vinyl Body
reviews.body: Not weighted, not soft, not easy to pose. Hair has thin and soft newborn feel, but smells overwhelmingly of baby powder. A bit pricey for what I’d normally gift to children, and not high enough quality for an adult. Looks realistic but doesn’t feel realistic. Body is full hollow vinyl.

reviews.title: Unique
reviews.body:
I liked this sand art. I thought it was unique. It looked very pretty in the house.

The quality was very good. It seemed to be very well made. It looked just like the picture. It really is beautiful. It is nice that you can pick it up, turn it over and then it looks different.

 I would recommend it.

reviews.title: Beautiful...
reviews.body:
I like trying to make it take as long as possible to fall.  My record so far (2 weeks of use) is that one day I started it up in the morning and it was still going the next morning!  I've got one that's been going for 6 hours right now, but it's not going to break the record.  The best way to do it seems to be not to use it for a few days between tries, that allows the bubbles to join up into bigger bubbles that work better.  And don't bump the table!

Regarding the way it looks, I love it.  The colors are so natural, it reminds me of layers of silt deposited at the bottom of the ocean.  And the gold sometimes makes defined layers and other times mixes in to turn the white orange.  So much variation, this will be worth looking at for a long time to come!

reviews.title: I really like this
reviews.body: Well made, really cool!

reviews.title: Just adorable and smells so good!
reviews.body: This really looks like a bottle of perfume! Upon opening we found a grape scented character. She smells so good! The scent reminds me of the grape scented markers from when I was in school. You also get tattoos and stickers, which is cool! My daughter loves this!

reviews.title: Kids will love this

The glitter will get all over the place, but it does vacuum up.

reviews.title: My kids LOVE Pikmi Pops
reviews.body:
I have two little girls who adore Pikmi Pops and they are loving this newest series of the Cheeki Puffs.

The blind bags come in a little "perfume" bottle. You'll get a super cute kawaii charm that coordinates with your puff. There is also a sticker sheet. The large blind bag contains your shimmer puff! The charm has a little string attached so your child can attach it to their backpack/purse.

The puff isn't messy and too much glitter. It's a light shimmer so it's not crazy. Smells great of course.

Overall, my girls are happy so I am happy!

reviews.title: So many stickers
reviews.body: My daughters love princesses so this is very nice for them. They love the huge variety. These stickers were very nice. They were a good size. You got a lot of them. They were bright and vibrant. They were really cute. The kids liked them. They stuck pretty well. It was a nice assortment. You can use them on all sorts of places. They really can make something look unique and nice. They were pretty easy to peel. They stayed on well. I was pleased with quality and durability. I would recommend it.

reviews.title: Beautiful, but thin
reviews.body: [[VIDEOID:1d8cbcbcefa93dfa8e39d06002a6470f]] I really love the design being a Disney princess fan. I have fond memories of these characters - unsure if they're for millenials since I don't think they'd recognize snow white or Cinderella.... The reason I'm saying this is because this little booklet was ordered for me, a middle aged woman and I'll say it's really designed for kids. The material is just ordinary sticker paper that's easily torn. The pages are very thin. The overall quality makes me feel like something to toss at a young kid. This won't satisfy a teen in my opinion.... Again, beautiful design, but I thought the quality really should be better being a Disney product.

reviews.body: This Buzz figurine is half the size of a regular Buzz. But that's actually great. My 4 year old girl can easily pick it up without straining with one hand. The battery insertion and replacement holds well and hasn’t fell apart with rough play. This comes with accessories to keep the playtime experience interesting. reviews.title: What you can build is only limited by your imagination
reviews.body: What can you do with 1005 pieces of MegaConstrux? You could use it to make even gnarlier kits, like Halo, Pokemon, Monster High and any number of other sets, or you can use your imagination and create your own designs. You also get Mega Construx Beyonders App for additional help and ideas. This is a hands on, creative based building set but if you need inspiration, you can use the app.

reviews.title: Mega Construx Inventions Deluxe Pack
reviews.body:
The Mega Construx Inventions Deluxe Pack reminds me of my childhood playing with Legos, back when I’d spend hours creating anything I could think of. The instruction book includes directions for only two builds. While you can download an app for more instructions, the app is only available for tablets, which seems like an odd limitation to me.

The pieces ARE compatible with Lego blocks and come in a wide array of colors. If you’re looking for a cost effective way to add to your kid’s (or your own) Lego collection and aren’t picky, this is a good one. There are also some more gimmicky Mega Construx pieces, such as flexible pieces and a necklace cord.

reviews.title: Awesome gift set
reviews.body:
My five-year-old is an expert Lego builder and builds tons of things from instruction books, but when it comes to actually building on the fly, his inventions tend towards the hilariously silly, and interactive things. This is the perfect set to mix it up with the existing bricks that he already has. I haven't had any problem with this brands bricks from any of the sets we have, they are all cross compatible with Lego without issue.

This set is just particularly awesome because it has so many really engaging parts, the clip that allows you to make something you can in theory put on your clothes or clip to a curtain, and the spring which allows for silly robots to take shape, were my sons favorites.

I love how this fosters creativity and extends existing toys to make them new and fresh again. This would make a really fantastic gift for a beloved person of Lego building interest. It comes in a series of bags and the outer packaging is a big bag, so it doesn't arrive with the box crushed and not good for giftgiving, as so many of the Lego sets do when ordered online.

reviews.title: Cheaply made

If you look at the photo of the doll you can tell that already one of her ribbon pieces of hair is coming out, and she's got glue marks on her head from where they were attached. I don't even play with her, either. She's a prop for when I teach English online and she's falling apart. All she does is sit in a basket, it's not like some toddler is mashing her around the house.

She says a lot of cute phrases, WOO noises, and plays catchy songs. I'd say 20 all together. But the actual doll herself is cheaply made. Half her hair is ribbon, the other half is printed on the fabric, just like all of her facial features. She looks and feels like a toy you would win at the carnival or a dog chew toy.

reviews.title: Very useful and well-made product!!
reviews.body:
A short time after I purchased my Nintendo Switch console, I also bought this Excellent item, the HORI Compact Playstand for Nintendo Switch (Officially Licensed by Nintendo).  I am very glad that I did!

If you think you will probably be using your Nintendo Switch often in what is commonly referred to as "Table Top" mode, then you will most likely want to pick up one of these incredibly useful Play Stand accessories.

The Play Stand itself is very easy to use, and it provides you with three different viewing angles.

And, because this Play Stand raises your Nintendo Switch up off of the table, you can then connect a USB C type connector to the bottom of your Switch, thus allowing you to charge your system, while the play Stand is being used.  This is a nice plus.

The HORI Play Stand is well-constructed.. and I would definitely​ recommend it to anyone who owns a Nintendo Switch!

reviews.title: Could have been the best keyboard for typing and working but....
reviews.body:
I was really impressed with the built, features, RGB color mode, Cherry MX keys options, price. I had ordered Cherry MX Blue (the click-y-tactile keys) which is a good option for typing. The "click-y" sounds are OK. I used my keyboard mainly for programmings (so don't know about gaming purpose). I love the default RGB lighting modes (my fav was breathing with slowest speed for no distraction during working); during night it would light up my working desk in a good way with a good vibe. It has robust and good front foot with a great angle (I also use an arm rest during prolong usage) for the wrist.

The built is heavy which makes it super stable during typing which I liked it. The keyboard layout is all right and the keyboard overall design looks great. This would have been the best keyboard for my programming/typing purpose with this such great price ($44.99) easily BUT randomly some keys don't registered even after I hear the "click-y" sound which defeats the Cherry MX BLUE keys purpose. Then just for experiment, whenever I typed, I painstakingly press each key all the ways to the bottom, way after the "click-y" sound, then I observed that the keys are in fact registering. But this is wrong, your fingers are way tired when it is pressed unusually up to the bottom in the mechanical keyboard. I gave it few days just to confirm what I am experiencing and just to give a chance to this brand, I ordered another of the same model. I observed same issues for couple of days. All the observation were concluded during and after prolong typing usage.

Keep in mind that I haven't tried other Redragon Cherry MX keys and couldn't comment anything about it. Also I could be the unluckiest one that got two defective keyboards among the sea of good Redragon keyboards (no sarcasm intended).

reviews.title: Great white keyboard for the price
reviews.body:
I've never owned a mechanical keyboard before, so I decided to branch out and bought both this keyboard and a different Redragon keyboard with red switches. I like both keyboards for different reasons, and would definitely recommend this brand to someone looking to get a good first keyboard.

The Good:
• It feels sturdy without being heavy at all.
• The keys are of good quality and are overall nice and smooth.
• Typing on it feels like typing on an old typewriter, it's VERY fun to experience for the first time.
• The RGB is awesome. It's controlled directly through the keyboard, you can set the brightness, and there's a TON of different effects to choose from (many of which include both rainbow and single-color options). My favorites are the soft rainbow fade one (FN+END one time), and the one that lights up every key you press for a short while for more subtle backlighting (press FN+HOME two times).
• I love the white color, it looks better than the black with the RGB lighting and the keys are really easy to read with the backlight turned off.
• The hotswappable keys are an incredibly neat feature and mean that one switch breaking isn't the end of your keyboard and that you could potentially mod this keyboard in the future if you wanted.

The Not-So-Good:
• People weren't kidding when they said blue switches are LOUD. I'm pretty sure that the metal backplate, while very durable feeling, is also causing the keys to make a slight ringing sound when pressed. This makes a loud keyboard even louder. I love the feeling of the keys, so if you're looking for a quieter but similar experience, I'd look for a keyboard from Redragon with brown switches instead. I've generally heard that brown switches provide the same tactile feedback while being quieter.
• On both keyboards I bought, the keys that have non-backlit symbols added to them have a rough texture. It makes me worried that they might rub off with use.

Personal Preferences:
•  I really wish Redragon had a white Tenkeyless keyboard with red switches because I'm finding that a full keyboard is a bit long for my personal preferences and that the blue switches are too annoying to for others to listen to. If they had this keyboard (the K552W-RGB) with red switches instead of blue, I'd buy it immediately.
•  Blue switches are such a joy to type on. Every key press feels so satisfying, but when it comes to gaming they don't feel quite right. You can make it work for gaming, don't get me wrong, I just think that this keyboard is best for people who don't mind really loud keyboards and want the best typing experience overall.
• It made my fingertips hurt after typing for a while, though I feel like this is something that will likely not be a problem with time.

reviews.title: Great headset minus the mic.
reviews.body:
The sound quality on these is great and setup was easy. They are very comfortable on the head and ears, the only small downside to comfort is my ears get a little warm but nothing uncomfortable. The true downside to this headset is the mic, it’s terrible. It doesn’t pick up lower sounds at all and cuts out frequently and if you have a deep voice it’s much worse. It also seems to produce some static when in use. Using the mic on discord is a no go. I’ve tried messing with all the setting in synapse and windows, and nothing fixes it.

Now onto my the USB dongle and THX Spacial. Just use stereo mode. I love the dongle and the all the other settings in synapse are great for dialing in the right sound, but THX Spacial is not very good. It muddys sound and just generally lowers sound quality when it is activated. Just buy Dolby access and use Atmos if you want surround for your headphones.

The build quality is great and feels sturdy. The aluminum Frame looks good and feels good.

Overall I’d recommend this headset as the usb controller is very nice and offers a lot of customization to sound through synapse. Probably one of the best headsets in the $100 range, as long as you have a different mic to use.

reviews.title: Excellent Gaming Mouse Mat With Color-Cycling Border
reviews.body:
If you have a Razer Chroma gaming mouse (e.g., [[ASIN:B01LXC1QL0 Razer DeathAdder Elite]]), you can set this excellent GOLIATHUS CHROMA SOFT GAMING MOUSE MAT to light up the border when you click your mouse.  If you don’t have a Razer mouse, you can set the mat to cycle 16.8 million colors around the border; to light up with a single color; or to fade in and out with a single color.  You can also set the mat to turn off when your display turns off.

All of the settings are done with the free Razer Synapse software (downloadable).  The colors are gorgeous--I liked the mat so well, I ordered a Chroma mouse to go with it.  The mat surface is an extremely “mouseable” soft textured fabric.  It’s also a very large mat.

You don’t need a USB 3.0 port for the mat to work--any USB port will do.  When I plugged the mat into a USB 2.0 port on a Win10 PC, it set itself up automatically, and opened a browser window for the Razer Synapse download.

reviews.title: Best budget mouse I've ever used

The mouse only weighs 85 grams which is crazy since mice that advertise as a light weight mouse typically come at a premium price. The button feel is nice and clicky with a great responsiveness. Overall the plastic also feel solid not cheap. I had no problems gripping the mouse and didn't accidentally hit the wrong buttons. The scroll wheel is surprisingly good. reviews.title: Get the razer viper mini instead
reviews.body:
Review update: I needed another mouse and this was sold out. The razer viper mini is very comparable so I bought it. It’s way nicer. Both are similar in regard to size and features but the razer is a lot better to use.

Original review comparing this wired mouse to clunky wireless mice:
I like this inexpensive mouse more than the last two expensive wireless mice I've ordered. I'm actually really surprised by how much I like it. This mouse was going to be my wired backup and now it's my primary.

Now , in retrospect, the wireless gaming mice I've been using for the past 13 years seem big, heavy, and clunky. This mouse is swift, comfortable, and I enjoy using it. Imagine that, being kind of excited to use a $30 mouse...

I do wish it had like 1-2 more programmable buttons on the side.

Lesson learned: You do NOT need to spend $100 to have a great mouse. Also, the wire isn't a big deal. It's lightweight and hardly noticeable; unlike the other (non gaming) wired mice I have experience with.

reviews.title: Good for the price; some nitpicks.
reviews.body:
Got this one for work. Eventually I'd like to get a Master, but that will have to be put on the back-burner for now. So far, I've used a basic Logitech mouse, an MX 518, and the Proteus Core in the last ten years. They all were my favorites mouses (yes, you heard me right: "mouses"), and I've been itching to replace the perfectly fine MX 518 I have at work, so I nabbed this one.

I think what they're trying to here is merge their lower-end mouses with their higher-end gaming mouses, so that they're able to offer their features to those on a lower budget. So far, I think this is fantastic, but that doesn't mean there aren't issues. It looks, when the lights are off, and feels like a $15 Logitech mouse. Which isn't a bad thing.
Every Logitech mouse I've used is far better than most of the alternatives. They make great mouse, and I will continue to source my non-trackball input devices from them in the future. On my desk, it looks like the old, beige Logitech one I had when I first started at this job, which most likely came with one of their computers years ago. The click isn't really sensitive as there's not much down stroke, and it's VERY low-profile. I use a fingertip grip and this thing can get a bit uncomfortable for me at times.

As for settings, you can use a few of the more basic settings you can from other gaming mouses. You can't switch between as many settings as more-dedicated gaming mouses, but they're still there. For a work computer, this mouse improves my navigation by a ton, but, like a said, the size does make it a bit uncomfortable for long periods of time.

The scroll wheel has no infinite scroll feature, which is the biggest physical downfall I found in terms of physical features. The side buttons are placed better than the MX 518 as I can reach them more easily, and the middle button behind the wheel acts as the tracking speed switcher. The scroll wheel can act as another button upon pressing, if you like, but I have that switched to off as I don't find it necessary for my use.

The light does have RGB, but I keep it on a cool blue all the time. You can have it set to either on or off, but I prefer on at a very low setting. I wish it would turn off completely after being idle after a while, but if you leave it on the "on" setting it remains on until the power source (i.e., the computer) is completely off.

If you think of it as a budget office mouse with neat little gaming features, then this one will serve handsomely. At $40 retail, however, I think it's priced a little high. Knock it down $10 and this will be the go-to mouse for all looking for a great mouse under $50.

reviews.title: HyperX Alloy Origins Core Tenkeyless, HyperX Red Linear Switch
reviews.body:
I’ve been using the HyperX Alloy Origins Core Tenkeyless Keyboard for a few weeks and I love it!

I have the Linear Switch (HyperX Red) version. This is my first time trying linear switches. The first few days, I felt like I was typing on the softest keyboard ever. I personally like how buttery and responsive it feels, but finding the right switch option is really one of those things you have to try yourself. I did notice that it’s easier to “bottom out” the linear switch versus say, a Cherry MX Blue switch.

I have a light hand and don’t do a ton of button mashing with the games I currently play (Warcraft, Paladins, SDV), so the Origins Core has replaced my daily driver, the HyperX Alloy Elite RGB (with Cherry MX Blue switches). I do miss the volume rocker on the Elite RGB, but that’s all I miss.

The Origins Core does have function keys (FN + F#) for volume, media control, and light profiles.

Getting back some of my desk with the Tenkeyless version is another plus, too. The keyboard is small enough that I actually would travel with it, if I were going somewhere for a few days. The USB cable is detachable, which makes it easier to transport.

I use this keyboard for both writing (at least 2-3 hours of typing a day) plus gaming. I like that HyperX has built angles of adjustability into the keyboard feet. I can have a 3°, 7°, or 11° angle. The keycaps are a little slippery during extended gaming sessions, but this hasn’t bothered me enough to replace them.

The keyboard itself has a good build feeling to it, and it doesn’t slide on my desk, even during intense moments.

I did try HyperX’s NGENUITY software to make my own custom lighting profiles. The software is only available on Windows, but the keyboard can save 3 profiles to its onboard memory. I switch between Windows and Mac, so I was excited that I could customize the keyboard on my Windows machine, and be able to use those light profiles on my Mac without needing the software. NGENUITY allows a LOT of customization; I spent a few hours playing with the different lighting options. I like NGENUITY more than Synapse.

I have one little quibble. I wish the lighting for the caps lock key was on the key itself, instead of above the arrows. But that’s a tiny little complaint, it doesn’t interfere with my use at all.

I recommend going with the RGB version; you can always set a solid color. The RGB lighting is so much fun, and I dare I say -- it’s pretty!

reviews.title: Aqua switches are the best!
reviews.body:
HyperX Alloy Origins - Mechanical Gaming Keyboard - Software-Controlled Light & Macro Customization - Compact Form Factor - Tactile Switch - HyperX Aqua - RGB LED Backlit

I just switched to this HyperX Alloy Origins Mechanical Gaming Keyboard with aqua switches from a Cherry MX blue keyboard. I really loved that keyboard but after trying this one I was sold. The tactile switches feel amazingly smooth and purposeful. The keys are solid feeling and don't wiggle at all. The keyboard itself is also solid and compact for a full keyboard. The RGB is also fantastic with each key able to be programmed. The colors are bright a vibrant. I'm Probably going to switch the keys for some PBT pudding key though. Not for any other reason than I like the way they look. The Aqua switches offer a shorter throw over MX switches 1.8mm vs 2.0mm. I don't really notice a difference but ok. One of the best features in my opinion is the NGinuity software. I hate the resource hogging software other manufactures make you use. The NGinuity software is a bit bare bones visually but offers all the same customization the other manufactures have while only using 26mb of ram. Icue and Synapse were both using almost 200mb each. I have now switched over to all HyperX for my Keyboard, Mouse, and Mousepad.

reviews.title: Thoroughly impressed with the quality of the shells themselves, which is all I cared about.
reviews.body:
Edit 18th June 2021: I can't really recommend this product anymore, not because of any lack of quality on its part, but because of the lack of quality of the Switch itself. The effort of trading out the shells is worth it if you only have to do it once, but the likelihood of your Switch or joy-cons having problems and needing to be sent in for repair (meaning you'll need to change back to the original housing or risk having them refuse to do the repair) is so high, that's it's just not worth the effort in my opinion.

Original review:

The clear replacement shells I received were so identical to their official counterparts that I'm convinced that they couldn't have simply been reverse-engineered. Whether it's legal to buy a decommissioned injection moulding die that was used by Nintendo, I don't know, but I'm not about to look a gift horse in the mouth.

I had none of the problems with button-fitting that others have mentioned, but I also used the original buttons, not the colorful replacements that were included. I had a brief scare when my + button wasn't working, but it turned out that I had simply over-tightened an internal screw--something I had no difficulty correcting.

I will say that I hadn't noticed from the pictures that the replacement shell does not include the front panel of the console housing, nor the cartridge slot cover. While the switch looks awesome from behind, I'm really disappointed that I can't tell from the front that any case-modding has even taken place. Aesthetically, it means that the console doesn't match the fully-clear joycons, as it's half-clear and half-black.

Nevertheless, I had to give this product all five stars because of its superior quality.

I wrote this review of my own volition and bought this product with my own damn money.

reviews.title: I want to like these, I really do
reviews.body:
I want to like these, I really do. When I first decided to do this swap to clear shells, I considered buying cheap Chinese shipped crap for like a few bucks. But then I thought, no, I want to do it right, so I spent $25 on these, $25 for a few pieces of plastic, that's half the price of the joycons themselves. But whatever, at least they would be  quality right? Unfortunately no.

The left controller went together fine. But the right controller? It had two spots where the tolerances were all wrong. One of the plastic supports near the plus button at the top of the controller, was slightly too short, so when you tightened the screw down it caused the plus button to be depressed. So I had to place a plastic shim in there too raise the circuit board high enough that it couldn't depress the button.

Next, the gap on the inside edge of the top plate where the tab on the black slide bar slides into, was too skinny in one small spot. Which caused the controller to not snap together properly, no matter how much force was applied. So I had to literally sand down the original black slide bar tab, to make it fit in the unusually small gap.

This may not sound so bad? Easy thing to fix right? Wrong. I didn't figure out the problem immediately, and there were two of them. The first controller I had done in less than an hour, the second controller took several hours to do, all time wasted, when I thought I had bought a professional quality product, because I definitely spent professional quality product money to get it. I won't be buying again.

reviews.title: No problems overall but there can be some improvements

Note I didn't end up using the supplied buttons as some said they don't fit right and I like the look better with the stock ones. Overall the quality and finish is great everything lined up well and no flashing or jagged pieces sticking out. Everything fit well and short of the overall complexity of the joycon design it went smoothly. Now the negative I really only have that it comes with 4 Phillips screws I have no Idea if these were suppose to be replacements or what as there was no label or instructions anywhere I wish they would just give a extra of each size screw used in case of striping. The other negative is the thin "gasket" that goes around the joycons joysticks is very delicate and difficult to install I just wish the new ones came preinstalled or just gave a set so you wouldn't have to worry about tearing the old ones off. Start to finish it took roughly 2 hours, it doesn not come with a screw driver so you will need a precision triwing and phillips screw driver, I ended up buying the tekton 2830 set for 9.99 and it worked perfectly. [[ASIN:B009MKGRQA TEKTON 2830 Everybit (TM) Precision Bit and Driver Kit for Electronic and Precision Devices, 27-Piece]]

Great addition to anyone's PS4 library. I had all previous ones on the PS3 but this is one of my favorite series and wanted the remastered versions.

It's 1080p and they fine tuned the controls and added newer difficulty like explorer mode (easy easy) and a higher one above Crushing difficulty with some newer trophies.. Word of advice for previous owners, it doesnt have multiplayer online for UC2 and 3. While some may see this as a negative, Naughty Dog wanted to focus on UC4 online. Visually, they knocked it out of the park. More vegetation, better shading, controls are better for example they took the gun controls of UC2 and added them to UC1 which is a major improvement since the original had wonky controls. More detail and the games look modern like they were PS4 games. This feels like a FULL remastered similar to how well the Grand Theft Auto Remastered looks like. The controls are PERFECT.

I bought a 2nd game and sent it to a buddy of mine that just bought a PS4 and never played any of the series since he owned an XBOX. He loves it.

Drake's Fortune yields the least upgrade, which is to be expected since it's the oldest, but by the time you get to Drake's Deception it's almost as beautiful at some points (*some* points) as Uncharted 4.
Do yourself a favor, ESPECIALLY if you've never played these, and buy this game!

reviews.title: Good for Giant Hands; Works Under Linux
reviews.body:
I am writing this review from the perspective not as a gamer but rather as a user who needs a comfortable pointing device. If you’re looking for reviews on what a wonderful gaming mouse this is, my review isn’t going to help you very much. If you instead want to know how it works for someone with big hands that does a lot of photo and drawing work, I have something to offer here.

I have the hands of a gorilla (seriously, I can palm a basketball) and I have had a terrible time finding a mouse that actually fits my hand properly. Because of this I have spent a good deal of time researching other options for pointing devices that are comfortable, including writing/art tablets, track balls, pens and more. I was not thinking about this when I selected this mouse; instead, I was thinking of my son who is a gamer and is always looking for a better mouse. I’m keeping this one for myself.

A lot of the reviews here mention that it is a claw-grip mouse, not a palm grip. I disagree, though I admit that I am not a typical user. It fits comfortably in my hand and I can rest the base of my palm on the desk and still reach the buttons comfortably without strain. This is good news for me, as most mice are small enough to require me to tuck in my thumb and contort my hand a little to get a good grip which just makes my hands cramp up.

I used the USB dongle to connect to my systems, not Bluetooth, mainly because my Windows computer acts funny with other Bluetooth-based pointing devices. The system saw the dongle, loaded the drivers it needed and the mouse was dead as a doornail because it needed to be charged so it still did not work. I plugged it in, set the mouse to use the USB connection and it worked somewhat as a wired mouse while it charged (it was communicating via the dongle but getting power through the wire). Once charged I disconnected from the power source and it gave me no more issues.

Operation is just as smooth and comfortable as I could hope. The buttons are firm but work well. I have tried all of the “standard” buttons and they work just fine – left-click, right-click, page forward, page backward and scroll. These are all I really need, though I like having the other buttons available should I need them later.

The precision is good and it works well for pixel-peeping when working with digital images. That’s about as close to gaming as I will get with this mouse. I need precision, not speed.

So, the main event for me: I plugged in the dongle in my Linux laptop and set the mouse to talk to it. I did not have access to all of the extra programmable buttons but the basic functions worked which is all I really need.

I realize I am not the normal user for such a mouse as this, but in my case this mouse works well for me and I am very pleased. It fits my hands very well and it just works.

First impression is that the mouse is pretty comfortable in my hand. It has a lot of adjustable settings and you can switch to 3 different profile settings with a tap of the button. It is very lightweight and the lights on it are pretty cool. Sometimes I get mouse lag when I try to move the pointer.
Con: I bought this mouse so I could stay wireless and game away without staying wired to my desktop. The battery life is horrible. I have had wireless mouse that I could play for weeks or over a month before charging or replacing a battery. This mouse has a battery life of 2 days max. If u are in the middle of the game and your mouse dies out it kind of sucks there is no clear indication that it is low and will die at any minute.

reviews.title: Bad Dongle.
reviews.body:
5 MONTH UPDATE: Changed to ONE STAR.  Now the thing has a double-click issue.  Started noticing it a few weeks ago where 1/10 click registered twice.  Today EVERY CLICK REGISTERS AS A DOUBLE CLICK. I've read some trouble-shooting items from their website...reset the mouse, checked polling rate in settings in iCUE, etc.  This mouse is functionally useless.  Piece of junk, and I wasted $80.  DO NOT BUY.  I went with a much cheaper Red Dragon.  Can't wait for it to get here tomorrow.  Never had issues with those.

3 MONTH UPDATE:  It has been three months and I figured it was time for an update.  The dongle has completely stopped working.  I can connect through USB and keep my iCue settings, but iCue doesn’t detect the mouse when connected through Bluetooth.  I feel like I wasted a LOT of money.  It no longer functions as a wireless mouse.  I think I am just going to get a cheap-o one next time.  Lame.
——-
Been using the mouse for about five hours.  I'm really impressed with the overall ergonomics.  Everything fits my hands great..Buttons are all easily accessible with no finger strain or stretching.  I actually didn't get this mouse for gaming, though.  I do a lot of video editing and typing and needed something with lots of customizable buttons to streamline my workflow.  Now that I got it figured out...I'm in LOVE with this mouse.

Prior to this mouse I've been using the Logitech Performance MX.  It was not great, but I used it until it started getting the double click syndrome.  I hated having to basically take my hand off the mouse to use the extra buttons.  I kept it out of spite because I spent so much money on it...hated to feel like I cheated myself.  This Ironclaw just FITS so much better.  Everything is so much more accessible. This is over half the price I paid for the Logitech!

The software, on the other hand, sucks!  iCUE is ridiculously complicated.  I was able to reassign all the buttons I wanted to change and I disabled all the silly lighting effects...set up a default profile that works with what gaming I actually do.  It just took WAAAY TOO LONG.  Even the $10 gaming mice from China with no English instructions were easier to setup.  Who designed this software?  Corsair needs to scrap all the "CUE" stuff and start over.

reviews.title: Great for meaty paws--but not for everyone
reviews.body:
I use this primarily for work, and I have a huge palm.  In those contexts, this is a great.  It fits perfectly, the tracking can be adjusted in hardware, and iCue is mostly optional.  I use it on my home PCs (the whole locked down work PC bit makes that hard to use on my PC), and I'm down with it.

The size of this mouse makes it hard to recommend to all or even most.  It also seems better for casual gamer than hardcore twitch gaming.  It doesn't allow for lifts without tracking (in general great for my usual work tasks), which can be a downer for some gamers.

I love the durability, size, dpi options, and all the buttons.

reviews.title: New favorite Zelda
reviews.body:
This is quite possibly my new favorite Zelda game.  I'll be honest, I was a little afraid of how drastically different this was to the entire series, but it was a risk that had great rewards.  If you're a Zelda fan or a fan of open world adventure games, do yourself a favor and pick this up.

My biggest complaints:
-Not many enemy types
-Some major fps drops in towns and in combat, especially when using elemental weapons (freezing weapons have actually caused the game to freeze for a second, ironically)
-If you try to 100% the game, it'll probably get a bit tedious as there are no temples, just 4 "dungeons" and 120 shrines which are 10 minute or so puzzles.

Some people would argue weapon degredation is a negative, but I honestly didn't mind it.  Yeah, it could be toned down a little, especially for the more rare weapons, but eh.

reviews.title: A new standard
reviews.body:
First of all, I'll say like everyone else, that the game is amazing. I wasn't sure I'd like it as much as I did but most of it works great.
Back when shadow of the colossus (sotc) 1st came out I remember thinking that this is what I'd like zelda games to be. And in many ways this game reminds me of sotc. Some similarities:
*The horses have a mind of their own which you guide
*Stamina limitations for climbing etc
*Gathering of fruits and animals (lizard tails in sotc)
*The Devine beasts can be liken to colossi
But while sotc was a simple game, zelda botw has taken most of those ideas and evolved into a much more elaborate game.
Weapons and shields break, don't really love it but sometimes you genuinely have to prepare your gear before certain tasks are done.
There are tons of things to gather.
Your preparation can lead to frustrating battles or comfortable victories.
Unfortunately the game is so open that the story is given in recollected memories and early in game discussions. This due to the fact that most of the game can be considered optional content.
Exploration is the heart of this game, there's always something interesting to be discovered or do, some alternative way to defeat a group of enemies... There's always something. It's great how lively this world feels.
A nice touch is how the climate affects you and the various ways in which you counter these effects. Too cool? Spicy food and warmer gear. Thunderstorm? Put away your metal gear. Its all interesting and fun, you sometimes need to explore more and discover new stuff that would make these trips more comfortable.

One note is the learning curve, because it's so open, you can find yourself feeling pretty overwhelmed by the enemies you meet up. While this is mostly due to not being prepared, you can die a lot and meet some challenges.

May edit this review when I experience more but so far the game is awesome, a must have for everyone that has a Wii U of Switch.

reviews.title: Best Console Currently Available.
reviews.body:
I'm copying part of a review I wrote for the 80gb model, then adding to it.

9/19/08
I've been a fan of the Playstation series since the beginning, and I proudly own a PS1, PS2, PSP and now a PS3. I'd have to say that this system is wonderful! I like everything about it. It's sleek, runs quiet, and pumps out an amazing picture (I"m only using a 26" LCD that supports 720p Picture resolution.) I'm a little disappointed that it won't play PS2 games, but I still have that system laying around. No complaints so far!

Update: 10/2/09
My system gets moderate to heavy use. Mostly as a DVD/Blu Ray player, though I've been playing way more games on it now that I have more time. It's still going strong. I recently upgraded from the stock 80gb hard drive to a 500gb one. The upgrade only took a bit of reading, and a couple hours of time (mostly for system back up and system restore... actual physical labor was about 5 minutes of work...) Over the past year, I've dabbled with the multimedia features as well as many of the fun miscellaneous things the PlayStation Network provides.

Over all, I consider this a must-have system for anyone who wants a complete media center. This will store/play all your music, play all your movies and even work as a PC if you install Linux (my next project, actually.) My only complaint about it is still the lack of PS2 support on this model. I'm hoping for Sony to get their act together and release software emulation via the PlayStation Store... I'd be willing to kick them some bucks for the convenience of playing my favorite PS2 games without having to dig up my old systems.

Update:  1/17/11
System's still going strong!  I've finished several games, and my TV has been upgraded to a 50" HDTV, and the picture is amazing!  That whole support for Other OS went the way of the warrior a while back, so those hopes were dashed.  I still stand by the 5 star rating, however.  The game catalog keeps improving, and the fact that I can stream Netflix and watch Blue Ray discs on it keeps it in the game.  I've been considering buying a slim model so I can have a set up in my room with the little TV!

reviews.title: I bought 3 mice, including my two old ones, and this one won.
reviews.body:
I got the E-3lue Cobra , this and Razer to replace my MS wireless mice at home and work.

All amazing mice.  3lue's thumb buttons are too close to you/palm of your hand and hard to find.  But for $11, that was great for work.

Anker and this were very comparable.  Both have great feel, quite, both have braided cloth cables, though this has a slightly softer thinner cable.

As far as design & LEDs, and Anker was better.  I like it's curve better and of course you can change the LED color to anything, and you can't change Razer's.

The buttons on Anker blew me away.  They are ALL comfortably reached and distinguishable with ease (and I'm not good at that).  AND they are programmable with a simple downloaded app.  That's not to say Razer's buttons aren't great, they really are, but you get the standard 5 buttons.  There you can 3 programmable thumb buttons that are fantastic for figuring out which is which by feel, and 4 buttons for your middle finger.

The software on the Anker also won.  The Razer mouse software wants to log into their server every time you boot (or always stay connected as another option).  As everyone else has said, WHY FORCE US TO CREATE AN ACCOUNT AND STAY CONNECTED??

Anker was going to be the winner in all fronts, including price for me, but alas I don't use a mouse-pad, I just put my mice on my desk with a wrist pad, and unlike the 3lue and Razer, the feet on the Anker would EVER so slightly stick to my desk.  Never while in motion, but when trying to point at something precise, I'd end up a millimeter to the side, and trying to move back would mean the ever so slight jerk to get it from the ever so slight sticking to move, ending the cursor yet at the other side of where I wanted to point.

So I'm going to keep the Razer as my gaming mouse... because its feet don't stick to my desk, it slides around quietly and effortlessly on my desk.

So, if you have a mousepad, I'd recommend Anker instead.  More buttons, better design, cheaper, no loggin in, great software, great LED colors, all around better mouse (though the Razer's cable is slightly nicer).  Otherwise, get the Razer.  If you don't have much money or don't care about the side buttons, then get the E-3lue Cobra Type-M EMS131BK High Precision Gaming Mouse

Ps.  The "programming" software you see everyone talking about is fairly useless.  You can't program the buttons.  What it allows is assigning a program to execute when a button is pressed, to assign different button numbers than the defaults or have a mouse button map to a keyboard (so pressing a button will press that key).  But you can't create programs or scripts.

It is as fast as you would want it to be. I can play my game, and if I need to pause so my boyfriend and I can switch to Netflix to watch a movie for dinner, it takes seconds. If he gets up and does something else for 10-15 minutes, it's an instant switch back to my game for the extra few minutes of gameplay, then right back to Netflix. No waiting, no saving.

Voice-commands I think are a little more receptive to males than females. If I lower the bass in my voice, it hears me just fine. If I use my normal voice it doesn't usually, It sees my boyfriend immediately when he walks into the room. Even if he's turned sideways, carrying bags of stuff. It knows it's him if he stands off to the side and coughs.

reviews.title: Xbox One is not your typical game console
reviews.body:
The fact that Microsoft has done everything it can to continue to provide updates and add new features since the Xbox One's release should be reason enough to select it over the competition. In an era where 1st party exclusives are beginning to matter less and less, you have to focus on the features of the console itself. In my mind, Sony has done a poor job with evolving the PS4. As of Sept 2015, it is basically the same device as it was when it was introduced. They haven't matched Microsoft in terms of features by a long shot.

Microsoft has added the ability to play Xbox 360 games starting November 2015 with over 100 titles that's set to expand greatly over the next 1-2 years. There's also talk of allowing backward compatibility with original Xbox games at some point. Being able to finally retire the Xbox 360 will be nice. The space it's taking up now will be a welcome addition to my entertainment center! That's in addition to the all the updates that make it a much more stable platform that better delivers on the promise of becoming an effective entertainment addition to your living room.

reviews.title: A worthy addition to the series
reviews.body:
I was a huge fan of the original Metroid and Super Metroid growing up.  The games were challenging, and games that require "skill" tend to be a bit hard for me.  This game, for the most part, is true-to-form.  I've sank a few hours into the game since receiving it.  Overall, the look, sound and feel is very much on par with the original series (with some obvious improvements as the technology has advanced significantly.)  The play control is very responsive - maybe slightly too responsive.  I really have one  gripe - and that's the need for repeated use of the counter-attack.  Metroid games have always required fast response times, and the need to recognize patterns during boss fights.  Each enemy takes several shots to kill (even when using missiles or charged beam.)  Most will wind up and charge you.  You can either dodge, and pick them off, or master that counter.  If you pull off a successful counter, the enemy is stunned for a period, and can be dispatched readily. Unfortunately, I find myself  losing the advantage it gives (due to terrain or another incoming enemy.)  The counter could be a great mechanism, but it seems to be a bit overdone.  Ultimately, this is a balance issue.  I feel that Samus's weapons are underpowered, while the enemies attacks are overpowered, and you NEED to rely on the new counter in order to really make progress.

All that being said, I got used to employing the counter attack, and the game is flowing.  It does a nice job scratching that nostalgia itch while feeling current (which makes 2 games in a row on the 3DS...  this and The Legend of Zelda:  A Link Between Worlds.)

reviews.body:
Fantastic! I never got to play the original two games but Super Metroid is my past, present, and future. I never got into the Prime style of games as much because I prefer the 2D sidescrolling type. Game has a very nice, updated look to it and I love the music. The new counter move seems a little gimmicky and overpowered at first, but later in the game is used less which I think is a fine balance. I don't usually enjoy boss fights but always seem to like the Nintendo ones; this game is no exception! These fights are a lot of trial and error as you learn boss patterns but dying in this game isn't terrible at all as it sets you back only to the previous screen or so and load times are fast; no simmering in your failure!

If you're a fan of old school Metroid or side scrolling games, I highly recommend! This was the first game I played on my new 2DS XL and it was perfect! I would suggest holding off on using the amiibos until after your first playthrough. They only give you extra tanks and such and I thought the difficulty without such things was very appropriate.

This is a great way for the kids to get some physical activity. They can really work up a storm while doing it, and they are having fun at the same time. Most people thing of video games as a very sedentary activity, but this is a way for kids to get some great physical activity. It is also great for the adults, too. It is a lot of fun, and has many great songs. The combination of sound and video make it a lot of fun. It is also great for parties. This very has also seen some improvements over the others.

reviews.title: A fabulous game that never forgets it's supposed to be fun
reviews.body:
There is way too much to love in this game.

It records you as you are dancing (or not -- you choose) and, if you have a good sense of humor, you can post it to Facebook, Twitter, or XBox Live (or not -- you choose).  You can play with friends.  You can play alone.  You can play online.  You want flexibility?  This game trains it and this game has it.  You want to just use it to work out?  Can do.

There are beloved oldies, like YMCA.  There are new hits like Roar.  The oldest song I found was from 1956 -- Just a Gigolo.  Flashdance, from 1984 is there is well.

You want to sing along?  Great!  You get extra points for that.

It's all about the fun.  Yeah, it'll tell you if you mess up, but it'll cheer you on.  It won't boo you off stage like Rock Band can.  If won't stop and say "let's try that again" like [[ASIN:B0057PERWU Country Dance Kinect]] will. It won't poke fun.  I suspect the design team never forgot that this is a game and never let it take itself too seriously. The result is that it is just fun.

If you've had trouble with other dance games before, you won't with this one.  If you love dance games, you'll love this one.  If you want a fun, heart-pounding work out game, here it is.  If you just want a crazy party game, this is perfect.

I just love it.

reviews.title: and it plays great. I actually love the 2DS
reviews.body:
I got the product on time, and it plays great. I actually love the 2DS, because it's far more comfortable than the 3DS or 3DS XL to hold, especially if you have large hands. If you buy trigger grips for it (available at gamestop, at least?), it becomes even more comfortable. I bought the 2DS mostly to play Super Smash Bros, but I have been exploring other 3DS games more than I expected. The 2DS is way better for Smash than the 3DS in my opinion, and the trigger grips make it almost as comfortable as a gamecube controller.

I still find it fairly pocketable in hoodie weather and winter, since I can shove it easily into any pocket. It may be a bit more troublesome to carry during the summer, but even then it fits in most of my pants, albeit barely. I don't miss the 3D at all, and in fact, the screen seems brighter than any 3DS I've used, at highest brightness.

All in all, I would highly recommend this product.

reviews.title: Owner of 3ds xl gives it two thumbs up
reviews.body:
Ugly.  When this was released I was totally perplexed and almost angry because it seemed so pared down and ugly.  I love handhelds and have had every itteration of the Game Boy Nintendo has ever made...some seemed mediocre and others great.  The original 3ds I got at launch was not comfortable to hold for long periods until I added the Nerf armor which made it larger.  My 3ds xl is the perfect handheld for me.....hundreds of hours on the system and it has held up very well.  It also has a ton of downloaded games on it (which sometimes causes me to leave it home rather than risk damage or theft). I got a great deal on the 2ds, used BUT after spending just a few days with it, I decided it is one of my favorites.
I am like many people who rarely use the 3ds option.  I found it completely nauseating on the original 3ds and only slightly better with the larger 3ds xl screens.  So, if 3d isn't important to you, this is a great system period.  3ds xl in comparrison feels much heavier after playing for an hour or more.  I am including this side by side picture of the size difference when the 3ds xl is open. The 2ds feels really comfortable for longer play to me and if you like or have or want games that use those shoulder buttons a lot it is a winner....very good size, comfortable and responsive.  Mario Kart 7 is a blast on it.  The lack of stereo from the one speaker doesn't really bother me....if I want stereo I plug in my headphones.  The 2ds reminds me of the Game Boy because it is large.  I am a big fan of the clamshell designs BUT there is no hinge here to get loose or break AND nothing wiggles and jiggles while playing race, fighting, or other games where you might have a tendency to jostle the system around some. That alone makes it unique and fun....I don't feel I need to be as careful with it, either.  This system feels solid. I don't have a problem with these small screens since there is no floppy hinge.  I do suggest screen protectors and a case. This will fit in cargo pants pockets and maybe the back pocket of guy's jeans. With the new price drop, I think everyone should consider it because it is a great system and the library of ds and 3ds games is incredible.  I actually recommend this system over 3ds xl....the price point is SO much better it makes this a must have and I have been totally satisfied with mine.  Hope you enjoy yours.

reviews.title: 6 months in.. an issue
reviews.body:
Edit to original review below

I've been using this keyboard for 6 months now and my letter M key will only show red.  It will not show any other color.  I realize this is minor and they keyboard still works fine, however, it's only been 6 months and things are already starting to not work.  Makes me wonder how many of the lights won't work in another 6 months.

So - I'm not sure my gaming experience is any better, but I do really like this keyboard.  I find the clacking of the switches really satisfying.  The RGB colors are nice.  Can't really tell any difference though in game performance vs a membrane keyboard.

reviews.title: Clicky and Colorful!
reviews.body:
[[VIDEOID:70a9d7fc077aa7e4fcd22d5f001a5734]] I just opened this thing out of the box and hooked it up so maybe I will have to change my review later if something unfortunate happens to it.
First, it's very easy to set up, no drivers or nothing, just plug it into a working usb port on your computer and you are ready.
There is no on-screen editor or whatever you want to call it, so you can manually mess with all the colors and keys on the board, its all something done with various key presses.
There are 9 different modes and 5 different gaming type presets already. So pressing FN +1-5 will change the gaming present while pressing FN + INS will change through the 9 modes, which I have uploaded a video of the 9 modes to see.
One of the first things I noticed setting this up is how stiff and sturdy the keyboard props on the bottom seem to feel. I always have an issue with those things breaking or just closing back up on their own on other keyboards, but that doesnt seem like itll be an issue on this keyboard. Infact, I had to use a cutical pusher to get the keyboard prop up off the back of the keyboard to use initially.

The wire is completely removeable, but I dont think the keyboard can be wireless as there is no sort of "antenna" you plug into the computer nor do you get one with it. There are nice grooves along the bottom of the keyboard for the wire to be fed through as well, straight out the back center, or down the left or right side .

It is extremely clicky. I happened to get the white keyboard with the blue switches and I am not at all dissapointed in the amount of clickyness I have from this, nor do I feel like I need more. Plenty clicky (I know people hunt that out specifically). Its even got a nice click bump deal before bottoming out the key :)

The top of the keyboard has a nice shiny brushed metal type plate that runs along the entire top giving it a really nice sleek design and extra durability in the board...although I dont feel like these things are used in a manner that would need something to prevent them from being...essentially broken in half....but I imagine that metal plate would help.

Overall, I feel really good about the keyboard out of the box. It has so many different color options and modes its so cool, just like I wanted. I love the clicky mechanicalness of it all and now I just wait to see how long it will last me! Hopefully years!
